The wealthy Merchant Antonio dotes on his friend Bassanio, a spendthrift who has depleted his inheritance. When Bassanio meets the brilliant, rich Portia, he asks Antonio to advance him money so he can compete for her hand in marriage. Antonio's wealth is tied up in ships at sea and, despite his Anti-Semitism, he asks to borrow from Shylock, a Jewish money-lender. Shylock agrees, but insists that if Antonio defaults, he carve a pound of flesh from Antonio's body.

This cat-and-mouse game is full of sly humor, sexual tension and suspense. In an underground vault in war-torn Paris, a more singular conflict takes place between an enigmatic female officer from the Ministry of Culture and the world famous painter, Pablo Picasso. With his work and possibly his life at stake, Picasso's negotiations are marked by mutual manipulation, unexpected revelations and a surprising final intrigue. (Contains Adult Language and Suggestive Dialogue)

The first world war is over, but some battles still rage on. Elevator Repair Service (GATZ, Sound and the Fury) brings Hemmingway's novel to life on a stage littered with liquor bottles and cafe chairs, as the story winds its way through France and Spain.

Charles and Joseph are having one hell of a year. When a prank-gone-wrong in a the small town of Nazareth, PA leads to the death of their father, the two brothers struggle with their health, livelihoods, and sanity as a series of unfortunate events spiral into operatic miseries. In an age where most people look to faith, finances, or even modern medicine to solve any unpleasantries in life, Sons of the Prophet takes a brutally funny look at unresolved chronic pain and the many ways we cope with the overwhelming.

Shrek the Musical, based on the Oscar®-winning DreamWorks film that started it all, brings the hilarious story of everyone's favorite ogre to life the stage.  In a faraway kingdom turned upside down, things get ugly when an unseemly ogre - not a handsome prince - shows up to rescue a feisty princess. Throw in a donkey who won't shut up, a bad guy with a SHORT temper, a cookie with an attitude and over a dozen other fairy tale misfits, and you've got the kind of mess that calls for a real hero. Luckily, there's one on hand… and his name is Shrek. Featuring a terrific score of 19 all-new songs, big laughs, great dancing and breathtaking scenery, USA Today proclaims Shrek the Musical, "Altogether Irresistible. A Big Fat Hit!"  Shrek the Musical is part romance, part twisted fairy tale and all irreverent fun for everyone!    Fun for all - Appropriate for ogres and ogresses of all ages

In the great green room, there was a telephone, and a red balloon, and a picture of the cow jumping over the moon . . . How do you turn one of America's most beloved picture books ever into a play? The playwright has brought an extraordinary imagination to the task, and has created a sparkling, magical musical that both elaborates on the original with style and wit, yet remains true to the simple heart of the book. You'll find a hundred surprises on the way to getting exactly what you expect!

"Pretty is as pretty does." Jack knows it -- and you know Jack! Old King is lookin' to get the best of him, but Jack's a clever 'un who ain't afeared of hard work nor Bluebeard Giants nor Raggedy-Bones his own self. He'll outfox that Old King, he'll win the heart of Old King's Daughter, and he'll carve out a new world with his own two hands. Drawing from the old-tyme Scots-Irish tales of the Appalachians, NCT's own Scot Copeland and Paul Carrol Binkley have fashioned a delightfully authentic gem of a mountain musical as sweet, dark and rich as the soil from which it sprang. "For the steps of a good man are known by the Lord...".

Sparkling like aluminum siding, this campy, caustic musical fable is ripe with adultery, strippers, murderous ex-boyfriends, Costco, and the Ice Capades. South Park meets Desperate Housewives in this big-hearted new musical comedy complete with a trashy Greek  chorus of trailer park divas, Armadillo Acres is Florida's most exclusive mobile home community until a stripper on the run comes between an agoraphobic housewife and her tollbooth-working husband.
showName: The Great American Trailer Park Musical

sSynopsis: An idyllic Forest of Arden provides the lush backdrop for Shakespeare's glorious romantic comedy of courtiers, clowns, philosophers and provincials--all bewitched by the trials and triumphs of love. Disguised as a boy, Rosalind escapes the perilous Court--only to find her heart in peril, as she instructs the very man she loves on how best to woo a woman. CST's Tony-nominated Associate Director Gary Griffin stages this tale of mistaken identity and misguided affection, following his wildly successful CST productions of Private Lives and Amadeus.

Sam and Eddie Sisson are more than just father and son; they're a crack team of hustlers always looking for the next mark. Sam, just a teenager who has practically raised himself, now wants to distinguish himself from his father and strike out on his own. Eddie doesn't want to let his son go without one final hustle, which could bring in their biggest take yet, but could ultimately tear them apart.

When Teddy comes to Celia's house to deliver a package, he doesn't expect to be invited for dinner. When he comes to dinner, he doesn't expect to be invited to live with her. When he starts to live with her, he doesn't expect to fall in love with her sister Amanda. And he definitely doesn't expect to be drugged ... or buried alive.     Elsewhere is a presentation of the Square One Series.  Created by the Bloomington Playwrights Project, the Square One Series is designed to change the game of playwriting workshops and to give small professional theatres a larger role in the national new works scene.

Joseph March is not a happy man. He's stuck in a dead end job. His boyfriend has left him for a younger man. There's a naked stranger in his bed. And, he's about to turn forty.     When his friends want to whisk him away for a surprise birthday get-a-way, what's a nice, gay guy supposed to do? Go along for the ride!!     If Joseph can survive the weekend, he just might find . . . EUPHORIA.
showName: Euphoria - A Work-Shop Reading of a New, Old-Fashioned, Gay Comedy

sSynopsis: Harry Chapin's Cotton Patch Gospel is the revamped version of this entertaining musical featuring the reverential retelling of the Gospels of Matthew and John in a contemporary southern setting, set to bluegrass music. The award winning musical is based on the book The Cotton Patch Gospel of Matthew and John by Clarence Jordan, a Bible scholar and Civil Rights activist. Tom Key and Russell Treyz adapted Jordan's writings and worked with the late Harry Chapin to create this musical stage version.

showName: I Am Who I Am: The True Story of Teddy Pendergrass

sSynopsis: Carnegie Room Concerts presents Avery Amero, mezzo soprano and Ronen Segev, piano.    Program  Bellini: Dolente Immagine; L'abbandono  Donizetti: Amore e morte  Chopin; Two Mazurkas  Tosti: Ideale; Non t'amo piu  Brahms: Wie Melodien; Von Ewiger Liebe  De Falla: Ritual Fire Dance  Schubert: Auf dem Wasser zu singen  Debussy: Arabesque; Beau Soir; Romance  Sondheim: Send in the Clowns
theater: Carnegie Room at The Nyack Library
sTicketPrice: $25.00 Adults; $20.00 Seniors; $17.00 Soiree Society Members; $35.00 Under 35 yrs; $5.00 Children 12 and under

sSynopsis: Gary Smulyan, repeat winner of the Jazz Journalists Association Award for Baritone Saxophone and the Baritone Saxophonist of the Year from the Downbeat Jazz Critics Poll, plays a surprising, witty and ultimately moving bebop counterpoint to the classical baritone saxophone of Henk van Twillert, internationally renowned for his performance of the Bach Cello Suites. For the second act: Smulyan in trio with drums and celebrated New York bassist Harvie S.

Meticulously faithful to the original music, the four member cast from the original Tony Award-winning Broadway musical recreates over 35 classic songs in an extravaganza that retraces the entire career of the greatest cultural phenomenon of all time.

The yearly holiday tradition that is The Broadway All-Star Holiday Concert is back! For over ten years, the dynamic composer/producer/pianist Neil Berg (The Prince & The Pauper, The Twelve, Grumpy Old Men, 100 Years of Broadway) has brought Town Hall theater goers evenings filled with Broadway hits, Pop classics and Holiday favorites. And this year will prove to be no different! Neil will be once again sharing the stage and co-hosting the evening with 5 time Broadway star, Trans-siberian Orchestra platinum recording artist and Irvington resident, Rob Evan. As always, current Broadway stars will recreate moments from the Great White Way as well as perform some of their favorite tunes. Neil will be at the grand piano in front of a 5 piece live band. This year a portion of the proceeds will go to benefit the devastation caused by the oil spill in The Gulf. Do not miss this sell-out! It's like having Broadway in your very own living room.

E.B. White's classic is brought to life by Theatreworks USA! Charlotte (a spider) and Wilbur (a pig) are unlikely friends, but when Wilbur faces the troubling prospect of becoming pork dinner, it's Charlotte to the rescue. Spinning words into her web, Charlotte makes a miracle of Wilbur and turns him into a sensation too prized to be eaten.

Dancing At Lughnasa is a brilliant, gripping family story, beautiful in its extraordinary depth and poetry and heartbreakingly poignant in its truth. Set in rural Ireland in the summer of 1936, the play follows the lives of the five Mundy sisters and their extended clan, exposing their long buried desires and vanishing dreams. Brian Friel's genius for layering time periods in this remarkable memory play won him a Tony award for Best Drama. It is a modern masterpiece which in the hands of The Schoolhouse creative team, will definitely be a remarkable evening of theater.   Not to be missed!

David Bromberg is a larger-than-life tornado of a performer who takes incredible joy from making great music with artists he admires (Bob Dylan, The Eagles, Ringo Starr, Willie Nelson, and Carly Simon to name a few). "He can hold an audience in his hand with a touching anecdotal song, and then set it romping with a raucous bit of raunch. He is electrifying" (The New York Times).

With influences that range from The Beatles to Mozart and from Duke Ellington to Woody Guthrie, it's no wonder The Dream Jam Band's debut album was named to the NPR Top 10 list of the Year's Best Family and Children's Albums. When asked how to describe their music, one member said, "a Marx Brothers movie that you can dance to!".
Under the wisteria vines and sunny skies, four women discover their true selves, rediscover romance and forge lasting friendships.

Eric Bibb has collaborated and shared the stage with such greats as Mavis Staples, Taj Mahal, Ray Charles, Ruthie Foster and Bonnie Raitt. Blending folk, blues, gospel and soul, be creates music that Time Out describes as "smooth, subtle, soulful and sophisticated...a beautiful and moving take on classic, coolly laid-back acoustic blues."

Tony Award Winner! Drama Desk Award Winner! On Broadway, Ben Vereen starred in "Wicked," "Chicago," "Fosse," "I'm Not Rappaport," "Hair," "Jesus Christ Superstar," "Pippin," "Jelly's Last Jam," "A Christmas Carol," and more! On TV, he was seen as the unforgettable Chicken George in "Roots." Ben has appeared on dozens of tv shows and series, such as "Grey's Anatomy," "Law and Order: CI," "The Nanny," "Touched By An Angel," "Fresh Prince of Bel-Air," to name a few. The program "Ben Vereen: His Roots" received 7 Emmy Awards. Don't miss this rare opportunity to spend an evening with Ben Vereen in this intimate setting for an exciting concert benefiting Westco Productions. VIP tickets at $150 include priority seating and a dessert reception "meet and greet" with Mr. Vereen after the concert.

One of Broadway's brightest stars comes to Irvington for an evening of show tunes and more! Sutton Foster won the Tony, Drama Desk, Critics Circle and Astaire awards as best actress in Thoroughly Modern Millie. She was recently seen on Broadway as Princess Fiona in Shrek The Musical, a role for which she received a Tony nomination. She has also received Tony nominations for her roles in the Broadway productions of The Drowsy Chaperone and Little Women: The Musical. Sutton starred as Inga in Mel Brooks' musical Young Frankenstein. She has performed in concert at Carnegie Hall and Lincoln Center. T-V includes "Law & Order: SVU," The Disney Channel and HBO.    Ms. Foster will be accompanied by Michael Rafter on piano.

The scene is a fishing lodge in rural Georgia often visited by "Froggy" LeSeuer, a British demolition expert who occasionally runs training sessions at a nearby army base. This time "Froggy" has brought along a friend, a pathologically shy young man named Charlie who is overcome with fear at the thought of making conversation with strangers. So "Froggy," before departing, tells all assembled that Charlie is from an exotic foreign country and speaks no English. Once alone the fun really begins, as Charlie overhears more than he should--the evil plans of a sinister, two-faced minister and his redneck associate; the fact that the minister's pretty fiancée is pregnant; and many other damaging revelations made with the thought that Charlie doesn't understand a word being said. That he does fuels the nonstop hilarity of the play and sets up the wildly funny climax in which things go uproariously awry for the "bad guys," and the "good guys" emerge triumphant.

Celebrate Tennessee Williams' 100th Birthday with the timeless masterpiece The Glass Menagerie, a touching tale of lost dreams, family bonds and survival. When Tom brings home a gentleman caller, his sister Laura is given hope. Their chance meeting becomes one of the sweetest and most heartbreaking stories ever told.

Former Caramoor Artistic Director and living legend, Andre Previn makes a triumphant return with the intensely musical and fiery violinist Joan Kwuon. This extraordinary duo explores the lush and scintillating sound worlds of three central works in the Francophone tradition.    Claude Debussy Sonata for Violin and Piano in G minor  Maurice Ravel Sonata for Violin and Piano in G Major  César Franck Sonata for Violin and Piano in A Major, M. 8
showName: Great Artists - Joan Kwuon and Andre Previn

sSynopsis: A chamber music dream team, Midori and Jonathan Biss return to Caramoor with internationally-renowned colleagues to explore these eternal works of Haydn, Schubert, and Dvorak. Perfect vehicles for these artists' brilliance and emotional sensitivity and depth, these masterpieces come alive in a Music Room event not to be missed.    Haydn Piano Trio in A Major, Hob. XV:9  Schubert Piano Trio in B-flat Major, D. 898  Dvorak Piano Quartet in E-flat Major, Op. 87
showName: Great Artists - Midori, Imai, Lederlin, Biss

Racoco Productions performs a marvelous mash-up of the Cinderella and Jack and the Beanstalk stories through a kaleidoscope of theater, dance, visual art, video, clown techniques, 20 lbs of flour and 400 square feet of crochet. Delightfully family friendly, If the Shoe Fits creates a magical dream-world of fairytales and our own flights of fancy.

Theatreworks USA presents eight fantastic mini-musicals based on popular kids' books. The tales range from If You Give a Mouse a Cookie, about a demanding (and hungry) mouse, to Martha Speaks, the hilarious story of a family dog that starts to talk, and much more!
showName: If You Give a Mouse a Cookie & Other Story Books

sSynopsis: Following its superb 2009-2010 residency at Caramoor, the Jasper String Quartet is the first ensemble in the history of the Ernst Stiefel Quartet-in-Residence program to be invited to extend their residency a second year. Continuing their tradition of presenting probing programs, the Jaspers return to the Music Room.    11/21/10 Program  Schubert Quartettsatz in C minor, D. 703  Kernis String Quartet No. 2  Beethoven String Quartet No. 9 in C Major, Op. 59 No. 3    03/19/11 Program  Beethoven   Quartet No. 3 in D Major, Op. 18 No. 3 C  Tao New Work Commissioned for Jasper Quartet through Brooklyn Friends of Chamber Music  Brahms String Quartet in A minor, Op. 51, No. 2

Westco is pleased to announce the return engagement of Judy Collins. Judy's previous concerts at Irvington sold-out quickly, so we urge you to order your tickets early and enjoy a true music legend in this intimate setting.

Emmy Award winning actress and comedian Judy Gold returns, following her sold out performance at the Emelin in May! Best known as the star of the critically acclaimed Off-Broadway hit show, 25 Questions for a Jewish Mother, she has also appeared on The View, Ugly Betty, HBO's At the Multiplex with Judy Gold, Tru TV's The Smoking Gun and hosting Comedy Central's 100 Greatest Stand-ups of All Time.

One of Broadway's leading ladies, you've seen her in Tony-nominated performances in South Pacific and Light in the Piazza, performing on stage at Carnegie Hall and Lincoln Center and now you can see her make her Emelin Theatre debut!

Among today's great vocal pop musicians, Kenny Vance and The Planotones have voices of original and inviting dimension. The group, Kenny Vance, Johnny Gale, Kurt "Frenchy" Yahjian, Jimmy Bense, keyboardist Chip Degaard, and Tony Gallino on Drums, redefine oldies with vocal authority and freshness. As exemplified by their signature song "Looking For An Echo", their material is influenced by the music of the 50's and 60's, but they consistently bring a unique and musically sophisticated point of view. In this sense they are classicists, opening the eyes of a new generation to a rich historical musical style. With their cool and sultry musical approach, filtered through a Brooklyn vibe, they give a gift to those who are discovering them for the first time!

Another returning star, Larry Stephenson has been known as one of the great high tenor singers in bluegrass since his early days with The Bluegrass Cardinals and with Bill Harrell and the Virginians. His crackerjack band exemplifies the best of traditional bluegrass: close harmonies, powerful picking and a fast-paced, entertaining stage show.

Laughter on the 23rd Floor is inspired by Neil Simon's early years churning out jokes for Sid Caesar's "Your Show Of Shows". This raucous comedy provides a hilarious behind-the- scenes look at the making of a 1950's variety show. The smartest, funniest and most screwed up people imaginable come together as a writing team under the pressure cooker of network censorship, the Red Scare, and a megalomaniac star! The result is touching and screamingly funny.   It is Neil Simon at the top of his game, and is sure to be an audience favorite!

You think homework is pressure? Just wait until you learn how the weight of the earth's atmosphere pushes down on you with the force of two elephants! Explore how Bernoulli's principle creates enough lift to make a jumbo jet fly or how air pressure can be used to launch a hot air balloon. Watch in amazement as our vortex generator creates giant smoke rings. Want even more pressure? Take a ride on our amazing Mad Science Hovercraft! Mad Science shows are fun and educational and this program will leave you flying high!
showName: Mad Science: Up, Up and Away
theater: The Bendheim Performing Arts Center at the JCC of Mid-Westchester

sSynopsis: Winners of the Silvestre Vargas award, Mexico's highest musical honor for mariachi, Mariachi Los Camperos presents an unforgettable evening showcasing Mexico's most enduring traditional folk songs. This Grammy-winning ensemble is hailed for its innovative concerts and the visionary leadership of its founder Nati Cano.

Hold on to your hats! Winner of five IBMA awards in 2009, including Fiddle Player of the Year and Instrumental Band of the Year, Mike Cleveland and his amazing band return to the Emelin with their unmatched energy, drive and power.

Expanding Caramoor's celebration of Mozart's more intimate music, Ed Arron and the Caramoor Virtuosi present a mixed bag of seldom-heard Mozart gems, including the Kegelstaat trio (the first work ever written for this instrumentation), set in relief by works from Beethoven and Arvo Part using Mozart's music as their source materials.    Mozart Duo in G Major for Violin and Viola, K. 423  Arvo Part Mozart-Adagio for Piano Trio  Mozart Trio for Clarinet, Viola, and Piano in E-flat, K. 498 (Kegelstatt)  Beethoven Variations in E-flat Major for Cello and Piano, "Bei Mannern" from Mozart's "The Magic Flute"  Mozart Piano Quartet No. 1 in G minor, K. 478

Celebrate the holidays in Mozartian style with the Orchestra of St. Luke's. Caramoor's Moz(art) series concludes with a scintillating program of Mozart's works for large wind ensembles, featuring the Gran Partita, his unparalleled masterpiece of the genre. Bach's Brandenburgs are a traditional holiday hit but these Mozart wind works find joy on every page of the scores.    Mozart Divertimento No. 12 for 2 oboes, 2 bassoons and 2 horns in E-flat Major, K. 252 (K. 240a)  Mozart Divertimento No. 14 for 2 oboes, 2 horns and 2 bassoons in B-flat Major, K. 270  Mozart Serenade No. 10 for winds in B-flat Major, K. 361/370a (Gran Partita)

Westchester's own Rat Race Choir returns to Irvington Town Hall to perform a special Holiday Concert with original band members bassist/vocalist Dave Chmela,Larry McGowan on keyboards, drummer extraordinaire Adam Snyder, and guitar virtuoso Craig Weinberg. The band continues its versatile progressive rock style keeping many of the old favorite tunes you remember, while adding new material to an already multi-faceted repertoire.

Perhaps the most adept and courageous choreographer in mainstream modern dance today, Pascal Rioult has a reputation for creating sensual, articulate, and exquisitely musical works. The Emelin's award-winning dance season begins with performances of Rioult's hauntingly beautiful pieces City, Wien and Views of the Fleeting World.

The Rose Tattoo by Tennessee Williams tells the story of Rose, a restless widow whose intense and absorbing instinct for love drives everything before it. The figure of this extraordinary woman dominates the small town where she and her friends are living and embodies the exultation and danger of unbridled passion. Her story, and that of the lover she chooses and the daughter she denies, are forged into a play of power, humanity and soaring emotion.

Snow White finds herself in peril when her stepmother, Queen Bella, is told by her Magic Mirror that the princess is fairer than she! Can Snow White, with the help of her friends, avoid a nasty fate or will the evil Queen and her minions triumph?    Presented by Missoula Children's Theatre Acting Camp.
showName: Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs

sSynopsis: Spalding Gray wrote timeless monologues whose words resonated deeply with audiences. In Spalding Gray: Stories Left to Tell, an ensemble cast performs excerpts from both renowned and never-before-seen work to launch the audience into the hilarious, heartbreaking, and remarkable life and career of one of the most irreverent and revered storytellers of our time.
showName: Spalding Gray: Stories Left to Tell

sSynopsis: Over the course of 20 years and eight albums, The Subdudes have quietly become one of America's national music treasures. The New Orleans-formed group is a living encapsulation of American music, a vibrant cauldron of sounds that stirs together meaty grooves and jazzy dynamics, soulful R&B swagger, easy vocal harmonies, cheeky rock 'n' roll attitude and folky social consciousness - not to mention some of the sharpest musicianship and ensemble playing you'll ever hear from any five musicians. It's tight enough to be loose, but never gratuitously.

Four-time Grammy nominees Trout Fishing in America make music for kids of all ages who take their fun seriously! Band members Keith Grimwood and Ezra Idlet have been creating acclaimed children's music for over 30 years, and have been described as "the Lennon and McCartney of kids' music" (NPR).

Be part of music history! This farewell tour is the last chance to see all four original members of Vanilla Fudge together! Tim Bogert, Vince Martell, Mark Stein, and Carmine Appice will perform their entire classic first ATCO Records album including "Ticket to Ride," "People Get Ready," "You Keep Me Hangin' On," "She's Not There," and more, followed by their other big hits which include, "Shotgun," "Season of the Witch," and "Break Song" among others! Vanilla Fudge became known for its own arrangements of contemporary pop songs, and was one of the few American bands which successfully forged a musical link between psychedelia and what would be labeled as heavy metal. The band rocketed to national prominence when it appeared on The Ed Sullivan Show performing "You Keep Me Hangin' On." With three hit albums in stores, Vanilla Fudge toured with Jimi Hendrix, followed by touring dates with Cream, and then a tour with Led Zeppelin as their opening act.

The Mermaid Theatre of Nova Scotia returns to the Emelin, bringing their acclaimed black light puppet show based on three classic Eric Carle tales, The Very Hungry Caterpillar, Little Cloud and The Mixed-Up Chamelion.

Greg's tight-knit social circle is thrown into turmoil when his offhand remarks about a female coworker's pretty face and his own girlfriend Steph's lack thereof get back to Steph. But that's just the beginning. Greg's best buddy, Kent, and Kent's wife, Carly, also enter into the picture, and the emotional equation becomes exponentially more complicated. As their relationships crumble, the four friends are forced to confront a sea of deceit, infidelity, and betrayed trust in their journey to answer that oh-so-American question: How much is pretty worth?

The Wailin' Jennys are Nicky Mehta, Ruth Moody and Heather Masse -- three distinct voices that together make an achingly perfect vocal sound. All established singer-songwriters in their own right, The Wailin' Jennys are winning fast fans all over the world with their powerful singing and thoughtful rootsy songwriting.

Pianist Thelonious Monk, uniquely creative as a player, wrote close to 100 enduringly beautiful tunes that are among the most recorded jazz standards. Gerry Mulligan was also well known as both an extraordinary baritone saxophonist and superlative composer/ arranger. For this concert, the WJO pairs these artists, inspired by their brilliant 1957 recording Mulligan Meets Monk.

With an illustrious career spanning five decades and 12 Grammy Awards, pianist, composer and NEA Jazz Master Herbie Hancock is an icon of modern music. His 1965 album Maiden Voyage is one of the most important recordings in jazz history. The nationally-acclaimed WJO will perform their interpretation of this seminal work as well as other pieces from Hancock's ongoing remarkable career.

The music of Miles Davis, Louis Armstrong, Dizzy Gillespie - and fellow trumpeters Freddie Hubbard, Kenny Dorham and Woody Shaw -- represents the very essence of jazz. Come hear the Westchester Jazz Orchestra as they perform new arrangements of masterpieces by these artists.
showName: WJO Trumpet Masters: Music of Miles, Pops and Dizzy

sSynopsis: A space-age mix of Blue Man Group, Cirque and STOMP...but clad in shimmering aluminum and uniquely its own! This stunning and incredible production offers a theatrical experience that is totally unique, combining amazing special effects, acrobatics, jazz and modern dance, puppetry, dazzling aluminum costumes, and phenomenal lighting.  An accomplished cast of athletic dancers and performance artists fuse industrial materials and movement to make a luminous and reflective extravaganza.  Join us for an art activity in the Youth Gallery from 5:30-7:00. $2 per person or FREE with your theater tickets.

The musical, complete with down home country humor, true emotion and even some audience participation, includes many of Patsy's unforgettable hits including "Crazy," "I Fall to Pieces," "Sweet Dreams" and "Walking After Midnight"...27 songs in all. The show's title was inspired by Cline's letters to Seger, which were consistently signed "Love Always...Patsy Cline."  Suitable for All Audiences.

An interactive one-man science variety show suitable for all audiences.  Doktor Kaboom creatively blends theatre arts with the wonders of scientific exploration, all the while keeping his crowds riveted with interest and rolling with laughter.    Join us for an art activity in the Hartwell-Chesbro room from 12:00-1:30 pm. $2 per person or FREE with your theater tickets.

Bored by his privileged but mundane life, Henry Flemming sells his lucrative brokerage firm to become a detective. On his very first case - to the horror of his wife, Karen, and his two crazy neighbors, Suzy and Stan - the Flemming living room begins to fill up with dead bodies. Karen is further annoyed when one of them turns out to be her father. Even though Henry keeps showing up at home every day more disheveled and beaten up, he couldn't be happier. Henry is convinced he's found his life's work and Westport, Connecticut is safer for it. The play is a spoof of the film noir thrillers from the 40s and 50s. Selected play in the 2008 International Mystery Writers' Festival.   Contains Mild Language & Suggested Violence

The Handsome Little Devils' Squirm Burpee Theatre honors the rich vaudevillian history of the Colonial Theatre. This company sings, dances, juggles, jokes, and does just about anything they can to charm audiences around the globe.    Join us for an art activity in the Hartwell-Chesbro room from 5:30-7:00 pm. $2 per person or FREE with your theater tickets.

Opera Idaho is excited to welcome back tenor Matt Morgan, along with internationally acclaimed soprano Rachelle Durkin, his wife, on Friday, March 11, 2011 at The Egyptian Theatre.     Rachelle Durkin will be making her first appearance in Idaho, though she is a frequent guest of The Metropolitan Opera in New York City, most recently appearing as Clorinda in La Cenerentola in May 2010. Due to her frequent appearances, The Opera Critic states that Durkin is "clearly the new star of Opera Australia." Time magazine declared Durkin a "down-to-earth spirit allied to a heavenly voice."
showName: In Concert: Rachelle Durkin and Matt Morgan

sSynopsis: Hailed by the Times of London as an "exceedingly yummy operatic cake," Donizetti's rousing La Fille du Régiment (The Daughter of the Regiment) is one of Donizetti's most cherished - and perhaps one of the most vocally challenging - operas. It includes the famous tenor aria "Ah! mes amis, quel jour de fête," often described as the "Mount Everest" for tenors due to its nine high Cs!

Renowned humor writer Patrick F. McManus' one-man comedy show, McManus in Love is appearing for two performances at the Colonial Theater.  After a 2010 sell-out with Poor Again…. Dagnabbit, Love follows the hilarious antics of Pat and his pal Crazy Eddie, as they discover their fear of the dark was child's play compared to their fear of girls.  Discover why your first date can warp your personality forever. The result is a hilarious romp through the maze of self-torture we all go through when we begin to date.  Actor Tim Behrens portrays the one-man cast of 15 characters, including a bat, a bear, a bicycle, and an even stranger assortment of humans.

The small town of Elroy, South Carolina is thrust into the evangelical spotlight when what seems to be the image of Jesus appears on a refrigerator in a trailer park. The discovery by Lou Ann Hightower, her husband Dwayne, and her best friend Betsy, sets into motion a frenzy of conflict, communion and good old fashioned commerce. When the National Investigator turns the appearance into front-page headlines, their trailer park becomes a Mecca for miracle seekers, soul searchers and disciples with a decidedly political agenda. At the urging of the towns business leaders, Betsy pretends to get messages from the appliance-based apparition, and the crowds multiply like loaves and fishes. Through the ordeal, the three undergo an evolution in their relationships with each other, and they are forced to come to grips with their lowly status in the caste system of the rural south. In a region where religion is as much a part of life as grits and cotton fields, God surely moves in mysterious ways.  Contains Mild Language.

Some guys have all the luck. That phrase certainly comes to mind when considering boogie-woogie and jazz pianist, vocalist, and composer Michael Kaeshammer.  As a 13 year old he discovered boogie woogie & stride piano as played by Fats Waller and Pete Johnson.  A piano playing jazz prodigy as a teenager, he has matured into a singer and songwriter of real skill and creative imagination. He also sings blues and jazz. He is noted for his polished but warm live shows. Factor in boyish good looks and it almost seems unfair.

Three points of view about a poignant drama are related by three characters addressing the audience directly. First there is Molly, blind since early infancy, who describes her world before and after an operation to restore some of her sight. Her husband, Frank, who pushed Molly into this operation, relates his view of his wife's journey into sightedness and his dealings with her doctor. Molly's once-famous eye surgeon, Mr. Rice, watches both Molly and Frank and reveals his opinion of them along with his own fears in handling the operation. Through it all we see each character's painful and happy histories, their memories and the events that led them to meet. Their stories interweave on stage, threading in and around each other's lives, until the unexpected and touching conclusion to this striking tale.   Contains Mild Language.

Three Ballets:    Brahms Waltzes    Music by Johannes Brahms (Waltzes, Op. 39 & Intermezzi, Op. 117for Piano)  Choreography by Peter Anastos  Costumes by David Heuvel  Felix Eisenhauer & Juli Draney, pianists    A ballet about couples.  All pas de deuxs that express the interior emotions of each couple as they explore their private worlds together.  Midnight Shadows    Music by Sergei Prokofiev (Sonata for Piano and Violin)  Choreography by Alex Ossadnik  Designs by Lito-John Demetita  Violin Solo by Jennifer Sullivan    A ballet to compelling 20th century music by Prokofiev. Starkly bold, modern shapes drive the dancers through a series of abstract yet dramatic configurations. Like a fast moving contemporary painting come to life.  By George!    Music by George Gershwin  Choreography by Peter Anastos  Costumes by Lito-John Demetita  Lighting by Shaun Sites    A speed-skate through some of the great American songs that are now considered classic. A jazzy and breezy ballet that gives the dancers a chance to express their fun side. Classic tunes and classical ballet unite for a rousing closer to this program.

The story of Aurora, the young and beautiful Princess who is condemned to fall asleep for 100 years until a handsome prince awakens her, is one of ballet's most cherished landmarks. We follow closely the 1890 scenario, celebrating this Imperial Russian fantasy with all the lively classical dancing and imagination of Ballet Idaho's dancers.
theater: Morrison Center for the Performing Arts - Boise State University

sSynopsis: Threads of Silk: A Gala Benefit Silk Road Theatre Project is an exquisite dining experience featuring cuisines inspired by cultures along the Silk Road. Guests can also enjoy luscious Silk Road Cocktails created exclusively for Threads of Silk by Adam Seger, one of Chicago's hottest and hippest mixologists. And while you dine, enjoy the fun and ever-so-lovely music of the Silk Road Cabaret Singers in a performance emceed by WTTW's Cheryl Hamada.    5:30p.m. - Cocktails  6:30p.m. - Buffet Dinner
showName: Threads of Silk: A Gala Benefit Silk Road Theatre Project
theater: The Narcissus Room -  Macy's on State Street

sSynopsis: The best band in the universe…ever. Starring the legendary Liatt Potter, Mike Banks, Larry Foster, Craig Green, Kevin Young, Dan Mihlfeith, and many, many more. This is hands down the best staged production this side of the Mississippi.
Another comedy about the Futrelle Sisters of Fayro, Texas.

In a career spanning over 40 years, Grammy Award-winning pianist and clarinetist Butch Thompson has worked with countless musicians around the world and earned a worldwide reputation as a classic jazz and ragtime master. The New Orleans Jazz Originals is a carefully assembled all-star lineup chosen from today's top players. In keeping with the spontaneous nature of this music, the band makes no attempt to copy classic performances; instead, these musicians are steeped in the language of jazz, and perform a variety of marches, blues, stomps, rags, and gospel music - a cross section of the New Orleans jazz tradition that reflects its leader's lifelong dedication.    Free preview lecture, discussions presented by industry experts that provide unique insight on performances, held 45 minutes prior to  performance in the Festival Lobby, near the Pasant Theatre's concession area.
sTheaterAddress: Michigan State University, East Lansing, MI 48821
showName: Butch Thompson's New Orleans Jazz Originals

sSynopsis: "One evening, after thinking it over for some time, Harold decided to go for a walk in the moonlight." So begins The Adventures of Harold and the Purple Crayon, based on the beloved book series by Crockett Johnson that follows the zany adventures of an inventive young boy. As it turned out, there wasn't any moon that night nor was there a path to walk on, so Harold simply drew them. And thus his journey began. Resourceful and brave, Harold creates the world he wants to explore, using nothing more than a big purple crayon and his sky's-the-limit imagination.    Age Rating: Ages 3 to 8
sTheaterAddress: Michigan State University, East Lansing, MI 48821

sSynopsis: Let Freedom Ringfeatures compositions by jazz artists who participated in the civic rights movement and shows how these works were tied to specific historic events. By telling the stories behind events such as Brown vs. the Board of Education, and Dr. Martin Luther King Jr.'s most famous speech "I Have A Dream," listeners discover how music can be used to send cultural and political messages of both protest and celebration. The concert is presented as a celebration of Black History Month, and features the music of artists such as Dave Brubeck, Charles Mingus and Duke Ellington performed by an outstanding group of talented musicians.    Age Rating: Ages 5 to 13
sTheaterAddress: Michigan State University, East Lansing, MI 48821

sSynopsis: Allan Felix has this thing about Humphrey Bogart. If only he had some of Bogart's technique. Bookish and insecure with women, Allan mostly resembles a disheveled, friendly old dog, until his hero - Bogey - comes to the rescue with a bevy of beauties, played out in hilarious fantasy sequences. It's tough making it in a world full of beautiful people, but if you can't be a hero, it helps if you have one...

A lively adaptation of this colorful American classic. Whether it's graveyards at midnight, buried treasure, or whitewashing fences, every day is an adventure if you're a boy growing up in a small town on the banks of the Mighty Mississippi. Best appreciated by ages 9 and up.

By Horton Foote    In a small Texas town c. 1987 at the height of the oil recession, the Gordons are land rich, cash poor and grandly deluded. A crisis in the family forces these self-absorbed, endearingly dysfunctional brothers, sisters, aunts, uncles and servants to agree on a course of action to steady that looks like a very uncertain future.

A wicked dark comedy of friendship, obsession and Southern sensibilities. Accidents seem to happen in the little diner off the interstate where three friends work together and keep a sinister secret. When one of them hides her own terrible secret from the others, everything beings to unravel.

Sidney Bruhl was once a celebrated playwright famous for his intricate thrillers. Now slightly past his prime, he enlists an ambitious younger writer, Clifford, to help him pen his deadliest tale yet. But as Clifford secretly begins writing his own version of Sidney's life story, and the quirky psychic next door begins to have real premonitions of murder, events quickly spiral out of control - who will survive? This is the most successful and popular whodunit in history!

A fun and provocative evening of short plays designed to showcase our student actors. They will run the gamut from comedy to drama to melodrama to farce. This will be a truly engaging and electric evening of theatre. This is a J-CAT YOUTH production (Grades 4-12).

sSynopsis: A gripping contemporary classic about a young man on trial for allegedly murdering his father, but one lone juror among the twelve is not convinced the boy is guilty. As he examines all the possibilities of what might have happened the night of the murder, his open-minded outlook convinces the other jurors there is a possibility of innocence after all. This engrossing courtroom drama will keep you on edge to its final moments.

A warm-hearted drama starring Elayne Wilks that chronicles the life of a writer/actress in the 1940's and 50's after supporting her family through the depression. She won Emmy's, Tony's, and the hearts of the American people.

And one of her friends, Holland Taylor, is doing her best to make sure we remember what Ann was all about. For more than three years, Taylor has been working on a one-woman show based on Richards' life - and what better place for an Austin debut than at the theatre Ann loved!
showName: Ann, An Affectionate Portrait of Ann Richards

sSynopsis: A wonderful comedy inspired by Simon's time working as a young writer on Sid Caesar's Your Show of Shows.

Like a fine wine that compliments everything, Susan Lubin's voice makes the transition from her spectacular opera career to the Great American Songbook with heady delight! Come ride along on this journey of a woman who has revealed in amazing joy, and overcome seemingly insurmountable obstacles, emerging stronger and more vibrant than before!

Smooth and delicious...are we talking about a fantastic champagne or Tony DeSare? Both! Since his very first appearance at ACT, audiences have been clamoring for have him back. The wait is over! You will thrill to hear his velvety, soaring voice, be blown away by his piano prowess, and swoon to his matinee idol looks!
Godspell is a musical based on the gospel of Matthew and told in parables.

Eric Clark, an acclaimed pianist will perform classic, Broadway and holiday standards. A portion of the box office will benefit The American heart Association.    For group tickets, call 551-206-9772.

Avenue Q tells the story of Princeton, a bright-eyed college grad who moves to NYC with big dreams and a tiny bank account. The only apartment he can afford is way out on Avenue Q, where everyone's looking for the same things he is: a decent job, a stable relationship, and a "purpose." Eventually, Princeton learns to embrace the ups and downs of city life and realizes that "the real world" isn't so bad, after all!

Grab the girls and throw on your best pumps for a hilarious and unpredictable evening with Bethenny Frankel of Bravo's The Real Housewives of New York City. This "Skinny Girl" television personality, best-selling author, and "Health Foodie" is always sassy and fabulous. Listen to Bethenny dish about her life, her work, and her passion for living healthy and living well.
showName: Skinnygirl Night Out: An evening with Bethenny Frankel

sSynopsis: Featuring comedian Kevin Kent in his quest to create a confectionary delight. The beautiful Spiegeltent turns into a den for intrigue, espionage and the ultimate candy-coated collusion. In the end, merriment and chaos reign, giving us all a License to Kiss.
showName: License to Kiss II, A Sweet Conspiracy

sSynopsis: Jennifer Holliday, who comes to San Francisco's Castro Theatre for a rare concert appearance this November, is a performer too multi-talented to be easily categorized. She is a Broadway legend who took The Great White Way by storm in "You Arm's Too Short to Box with God" and later changed theatre history with her iconic, Tony Award winning performance as Effie White in Dreamgirls. She is an unparalleled R&B songstress who scored smash hits with classic tunes such as "And I Am Telling You I'm Not Going," "Hard Time for Lovers, "No Frills Love," and "Heart on the Line." She is a spiritually thrilling gospel singer who performed powerful duets with the likes of Luther Vandross, delivering a rendition of "His Eye is on The Sparrow" that is said to have left Paul Simon speechless. She is an indelible contributor to many of television's greatest moments, offering astonishing performances of her signature tunes on the Grammy and BET awards, and creating memorable characters on shows such as Touched by An Angel and Ally McBeal. She is a dedicated and tireless humanitarian, dedicating countless hours (and countless performances) to the fight against AIDS. Miss Holliday's concert is sure to be a thrilling experience for any fan who has been touched by any of Miss Holliday's many gifts.

sSynopsis: An Evening With Sutton Foster is a one woman cabaret show by the Tony award-winning Broadway performer.

Agrippina wants her rotten son to be the emperor of Rome. What's a mother to do? She promises anything to everyone standing in her way: Nero himself, an ambitious courtesan, a general, a couple of fawning sycophants, and half the Roman  Senate. Also her husband, current emperor Claudius. The numbers are staggering. No, really. Handel's music soars. Come delight in his fresh  musical invention and some crazy, hothouse humanity.

"Rehearsal at Theresienstadt, 1944"     Rising out of the very depths and horrifying moral chaos of World War II, The Emperor of Atlantis, or Death Quits is both a biting meditation on the fragility and brutality of existence and a wry and ironic celebration of life's purposes. A look at the tragic performance history of the opera and its subsequent reverberations--illustrated by photographs, some of the compelling visual art created at the camp, and music from the opera itself, other compositions of Ullmann and an excerpt from Richard Beaudoin's commissioned piece to be performed with Emperor. He will be joined by members of the BLO creative team and cast members.
showName: Signature Series  the MFA:  The Emperor of Atlantis, or Death Quits
theater: Museum of Fine Arts - Remis Auditorium

sSynopsis: The magical worlds of sleep, night and extravagant dream that enrich both Shakespeare's play and Britten's opera A Midsummer Night's Dream are brought together in an evocative collage. showName: Signature Series  the MFA: A Midsummer Night's Dream
theater: Museum of Fine Arts - Remis Auditorium

Whether you are a long-time SpeakEasy supporter, or just a fan of musical theatre, you are sure to enjoy this one-of-a-kind musical event.

The London Times hails the new show "a five star hit, astonishingly powerful and as good as the original." The Western Mail says "an outstanding success - the best version yet."

sSynopsis: More than fifty years ago one musical changed theater forever. Now it's back on Broadway mesmerizing audiences once again.    From the first note to the final breath, West Side Story soars as the greatest love story of all time. Directed by its two-time Tony Award-winning librettist Arthur Laurents, West Side Story remains as powerful, poignant and timely as ever.    The new Broadway cast album of West Side Story recently won the 2010 Grammy Award for Best Musical Show Album. The Bernstein and Sondheim score is considered to be one of Broadway's finest and features such classics of the American musical theatre as "Something's Coming," "Tonight," "America," "I Feel Pretty" and "Somewhere."    "So exciting it makes you ache with pleasure."   - John Lahr, The New Yorker

This landmark musical won the Theatre World award plus five Tony Awards and five Drama Desk Awards for its once-upon-a-time-style telling of Pippin, son of Charlemagne. Its coming-of-age story takes Pippin from being a naïve young prince to his kingship where he struggles to rule a kingdom without warfare. The memorable songs of the show have been recorded by scores of recording artists and its concepts and choreography made a Broadway legend of Bob Fosse.

sSynopsis: Shrek The Musical, based on the Oscar®-winning DreamWorks film that started it all, brings the hilarious story of everyone's favorite ogre to life on the stage. In a faraway kingdom turned upside down, things get ugly when an unseemly ogre - not a handsome prince - shows up to rescue a feisty princess. Throw in a donkey who won't shut up, a bad guy with a short temper, a cookie with an attitude and over a dozen other fairy tale misfits, and you've got the kind of mess that calls for a real hero. Luckily, there's one on hand... and his name is Shrek.     Featuring a terrific score of 19 all-new songs, big laughs, great dancing and breathtaking scenery, USA Today proclaims Shrek The Musical, "Altogether irresistible. A big fat hit!" Shrek The Musical is part romance, part twisted fairy tale and all irreverent fun for everyone!

Stomp is explosive, provocative, sophisticated, sexy, utterly unique and appeals to audiences of all ages. The international percussion sensation has garnered an armful of awards and rave reviews, and has appeared on numerous national television shows. The eight-member troupe uses everything but conventional percussion instruments - matchboxes, wooden poles, brooms, garbage cans, Zippo lighters, hubcaps - to fill the stage with magnificent rhythms. As USA Today says, "STOMP finds beautiful noises in the strangest places." STOMP. See what the noise is about.

As one of the American Theatre's quintessential leading ladies, Tony winner Betty Buckley has been dazzling audiences across the globe for decades. In this unique, interactive event, attendees will be able to request their favorite Broadway hits to be performed live on stage! Ms. Buckley's incomparable presence is a humbling addition to our Monday night event series - we are honored to be able to present her in this very special concert in early 2011.    Seth Rudetsky is the Broadway host, seven days a week, on Sirius Satellite Radio. As a pianist, Seth has played for more than a dozen Broadway shows including Ragtime, Les Miserables, and Phantom of the Opera.     Tickets go on sale to the general public on Tuesday, September 7 at 10:00am.

sSynopsis: City favorites Simonson and Hatcher celebrate Pittsburgh-born comic playwright George S. Kaufman by placing him at the center of his own Kaufman-like plot. The famed dramatist returns to his Pittsburgh childhood home to cure a case of writer's block, only to find himself foiled at every turn by slamming doors, mistaken identities, and a hilarious assortment of eccentric locals.

"Daring, savagely incisive," says LA Times. Harry Hart-Browne stars in Tony Abatemarco's critically acclaimed one-man play about a gay youth's sexual coming of age. "An affirmation of individualism and tolerance." (LA Weekly). Set on Long Island in the '60's, Cologne deals with the dire consequences an adolescent boy suffers when he tries to avoid suspicion about his sexual preference by arranging for the bashing of another boy with whom he'd been involved. Abatemarco's powerful story is as relevant today amidst the headlines about bullying and the suicides of gay teens as when it was written. "Strikingly sensuous," (NY Times). Rated R for mature themes and situations. Harry Hart-Browne (Seinfeld, LA Law, Night Court, Married…With Children, Hill Street Blues) has received eleven awards for his acting work and starred in the Off-Broadway classic The Hot l Baltimore. He helped pioneer the personal story solo play with his ground-breaking Pardon Me, I'm Having an Emotion in 1978. Award-winning director-writer Tony Abatemarco recently directed Catwalk Confidential in London's West. Prior to that he directed Julie Harris in Lucifer's Child on Broadway and for A & E TV; other directing credits: Mark Taper Forum, Pasadena Playhouse, Santa Fe Stages, La Mama, Theatre Grévin, Paris.
showName: Cologne Or The Ways Evil Enters The World

sSynopsis: The Duke's authoritarian deputy, Angelo, is hell-bent on stamping out moral decay. He reactivates outdated Draconian laws and aims his arrogant crosshairs at a young man whose fiancée is pregnant, sentencing him to death. Angelo is sternly incorruptible--until he meets Isabela, a beautiful religious novice whose desirability arouses him. Flavored with live music by the mariachi band Las Colibri, Rauch's vigorous, modern production of Shakespeare's tragicomedy reveals what can happen when sex, religion and politics collide.    Shakespeare's tragicomedy explores restraint and lack of restraint. It is a compelling mix of the things we're still obsessed with--morality, religion and politics. It is best suited for mature 14-year-olds and up. Prologue recommended. Please view our full age recommendation here.    Schedule Varies, see website.

A sultry summer in 1930s Alabama suddenly shifts for Scout, when her father, Atticus Finch, defends a black man unjustly accused of raping a white woman. Atticus' courageous act unleashes the town's wrath and endangers his family. Ultimately, the trial's tragic aftermath causes a ripple of change in a country town locked in old ways--and has an indelible effect on a young girl's understanding of right and wrong. Based on the Pulitzer Prize-winning novel that, 50 years later, still prods our national moral conscience.    Suitable and highly recommended for students 12 and up. Prologue recommended. Please view our full age recommendation here.    Schedule Varies, see website.

A concert reading of the winner of ANMT's 2010 Search for New Musicals: a loving tribute to the operettas of Gilbert & Sullivan, set to the music by Arthur Sullivan (with book and lyrics by Charles Veley).    Gilbert & Sullivan operettas are arguably still the most widely-performed on the planet, more than a century after delighting their first audiences. This tribute follows happily in the G&S tradition, taking a lighthearted view of contemporary follies and foibles. Like the G&S stories, G&S On Wall $treet starts with a somewhat absurd premise, propelling the characters through topsy-turvy turns of events and arriving at a logical but hilarious conclusion. Sullivan's wonderful and entrancing melodies lift the mood, to borrow phrases from both contemporary Wall Street and The Mikado, "to a height of irrational exuberance that few can scale."

In 1940, singer Machito and trumpet player Mario Bauzá arrived in New York City from La Habana, paving the way for the encounter between Cuban percussionist Chano Pozo and the great American jazz trumpeter Dizzy Gillespie. And so "Latin Jazz" is born. This original cabaret celebrates artists from this genre such as Tito Puente and Mario Bauzá, and explores the powerful cultural and social fusion that took place in the Big Apple. In Spanish with English surtitles.
Interactive demonstrations in castanets, fans and zapateo for children and the entire family led by Lourdes Elías, co-director of the Spanish Dance Society, and other local flamenco artists.

In A Raisin in the Sun, a family's shared dream for a better life may be, not only deferred, but destroyed by conflicting aspirations, betrayal and racism. Lorraine Hansberry's classic drama continues to shine an unflinching spotlight on America's struggle to overcome its past, while paying tribute to those courageous enough to shape a future filled with an abiding faith, in the decency of the human spirit.

sSynopsis: Currently playing on Broadway, this Tony Award-winning musical stars Sahr Gaujah as Fela Anikulapo-Kuti. Fela! tells the true story of Nigerian musicial Fela Kuti through the Afrobeat music he used to inspire a generation to fight for civil rights. Don't miss the opportunity to see this popular production in Washington, D.C.!
theater: Shakespeare Theatre Company - Sidney Harman Hall

sSynopsis: Fanny Brice was a unique American performer, and undeniably a great one. She conquered burlesque, vaudeville, the Ziegfeld Follies, radio and films, introduced hit songs that are still cabaret classics today, and excelled at sketch comedy and dancing. Yet because her movie appearances were few, the public's memory of Fanny is fading.     One Night with Fanny Brice by Chip Deffaa brings Fanny back to life! Mysteriously returned to the stage for "one night" in front of a curious audience, Fanny tells her story with colorful anecdotes - all true! - and best of all, Fanny's greatest song hits, which just happen to be some of the best and most beloved melodies from the years between the World Wars, including "I'm Always Chasing Rainbows," "Won't You Come Home, Bill Bailey?", "Will You Love Me In December As You Do In May?", "Be My Little Baby Bumble Bee," "Rose Of Washington Square," "You Made Me Love You," "Second Hand Rose," "A Pretty Girl Is Like A Melody," "After You've Gone," and her calling card, "My Man."
theater: The American Century Theater at Gunston Arts Center

sSynopsis: One show only! An NEA Jazz Master and three-time Grammy Award winner, composer and pianist Ramsey Lewis has been referred to as "the great performer," a title reflecting his performance style and musical selections which display his early gospel playing and classical training along with his love of jazz and other musical forms. He brings Proclamation of Hope, the large-scale multimedia composition for wind ensemble, rhythm section, and voice commissioned by and premiered at the Ravinia Festival in 2009. Composed by Lewis and scored by Scott Hall, the work celebrates one of the most famous Americans ever, Abraham Lincoln, on the occasion of the 200th anniversary of his birth. The Chicago Tribune calls it "a persuasive merger of jazz and classical idioms" and "some of the most eloquent music of Lewis's career."
theater: The Kennedy Center- The Concert Hall

sSynopsis: Spend a star struck Sunday afternoon with Broadway legend Stephen Sondheim in a lively chat hosted by The Washington Post theater critic Peter Marks! Winner of eight Tony Awards, the Pulitzer Prize, an Academy Award, Grammy Awards and countless additional honors, this witty, literary lion of American theater has penned some of the most memorable Broadway classics of the last 50 years, from writing the lyrics for West Side Story and Gypsy, to composing both music and lyrics for his crowning achievements including Company, Sunday in the Park with George, Sweeney Todd and Assassins. And Sondheim has stories to tell, as evidenced by his critically acclaimed new memoir Finishing the Hat: "Brilliant...Sondheim's anecdotes involving legendary showbiz names are historical footnotes to some of the last century's great musicals" (Paul Simon, The New York Times Book Review).
showName: Sunday at Strathmore with Stephen Sondheim

sSynopsis: Inspired by their rich heritage of Celtic music and fired by the strength and vibrancy of today's Scottish cultural scene, which indeed they have done much to create and fuel, they have led, and been at the forefront, of a great revival in Scottish music. Named after the Glasgow suburb of Battlefield, where the group was formed by four student friends, Battlefield Band have been on the world's roads for just on 30 years now, distilling their own unique form of the Scottish spirit and bottling it in concert and onto disc - Germany, Hong Kong, Australia, New Zealand, Italy, Austria, Switzerland, Holland, Syria, Jordan, India, Sri Lanka, Egypt, U.S.A., Canada, Uzbekistan and the U.K. They have broken down barriers and pioneered many new directions which others have followed. Angry, joyful, raucous, contemplative, their music is most importantly - accessible to all.    During those years there have obviously been line-up changes and indeed the band are remarkable for the smooth and organic way in which these changes have taken place. Musical evidence of these changes can be heard on their many albums made over the years.

Boo Bess The Baroness is returning with her unique brand of burlesque last seen in our Summer Shows, While Dangrr Doll is putting everything at risk to make her debut with us as well as Rita Men Weep who is fresh out of the Fringe Festival with the award winning show Friends of Dorothy. Nelson Lugo the co-creator of Epic Win Burlesque is back to astound and amaze and Liz Miele from Comedy Central and Caroline's will be bringing the laughs.
