Women on the Edge is a dramatic stage play, depicting the lives of 10 women who find themselves on the brink of self-actualization concerning their past or present relationships. Weaving together distinct tales for each woman, the play opens with four young women discussing their emotions as they reminisce about love lost and ends with all the women finding fulfillment when they come to the aid of a troubled Sara, who after many years of abuse, has finally taken matters into her own hands.    What lies between is the sharing of stories about being on the verge of a breakthrough or a breakdown, expressed through monologue, prose, poetry, song and interpretive dance. Women on the Edge is a strikingly vivid reminder that before you can have a loving relationship with someone else, you must first form a loving relationship with your inner and spiritual self.      Uplifting and poignant, this play goes back to the basics and shows how the bonding of women - young and old - is as crucial to development as air, food and water. Women on the Edge breathes life into the notion that united we stand, divided we fall.

A new spin on the classic story of Alice and her Looking-Glass world, Wonderland is about a modern-day woman who goes on a life-changing adventure far below the streets of New York City, where a colorful cast of strange but familiar characters help her rediscover what's really important. Featuring a fresh, contemporary pop score from the creator of Jekyll and Hyde, Wonderland arrives on Broadway this spring following two sold-out national stage premieres.
showName: Wonderland: A New Alice. A New Musical

The New York Times describes his violin as having an "old-fashioned rhapsodic style, magnified by Kutik's rich, sweet tone." His superb repertoire encompasses composers from Bach to Brahms to Previn and Martino.

Yvonne Meier is a two-time Bessie award-winner, most recently for Stolen, which premiered at Danspace Project in 2009. She "acts as eccentric drill sergeant" (Claudia LaRocco, New York Times) and gives the performers distillates from (often absurd) human conditions, which Meier calls "scores." She returns to Danspace to present new improvisitory inputs for musicians and dancers. The performers translate the scores in real time into complex music and dance, resulting in exciting and dramatic friction between the dancers and musicians.
sTheaterAddress: 2nd Ave at 10th Street, New York, NY

sSynopsis: A poignant examination of how war affects the mind of a solider, Sophocles's tragedy speaks directly to our times. The legendary Greek warrior Ajax is second only to Achilles in greatness and though they are victorious as the city of Troy falls to the Greeks, Ajax struggles under the weight of psychological and physical injuries, trying to maintain his dignity, identity, and honor.  His inability to cope with the trauma of war, the shifting moral landscapes as the rules change from war to peacetime, raises timeless questions about what happens when a warrior has to return to civilian life following deployment and how society acknowledges its responsibility for the well-being of its soldiers.  The production further examines society's role in accepting returning heroes into a peacetime community.

Years before "Dancing with the Stars" and "So You Think You Can Dance" turned Ballroom Dancing into must-see TV, Burn the Floor was blazing a new dance trail and igniting stages around the globe. In Burn the Floor, Ballroom Dance is totally reinvented. All the dance styles are refreshed and invigorated and leave audiences grinning with delight and screaming for more. You see and feel, live on stage, all the passion, drama and sizzling excitement of 20 gorgeous world champion dancers in a true theatrical experience, a performance with a grace and athleticism that The New York Times calls, "Dazzling!" and The Times (London) calls "the summer's hottest ticket"! Anya Garnis and Pasha Kovalev of TV's "So You Think You Can Dance" will join the touring company.

sSynopsis: Through physical storytelling, moments of story are crystallized as the cast imagines the warrior Odysseus explaining to his son what it means to go to war. The primary focus is on physical manifestations of the actors, who have rigorously trained since last summer to perfect their craft. This visual experience for the audience allows for a deeper connections to the stage, celebrating the imagination of both actors and audience...  to complete the story. The style fuses dance, theatre, mime, improvisation, music, drumming, and visual artistic elements. The direction team includes professors Kate Amory and Celena Sky April, with Jesse Mangan '11, who earned a Summer Artistic Development Grant from the Center for Creative and Performing Arts last year to study PUSH Physical Theatre in New York. Says Mangan "it's a post-apocalyptic ancient Greece meets punk rock with a Cirque du Soleil twist."
theater: Salem State College Callan Studio Theatre

sSynopsis: Dramatizing the famous passage from the novel that imagines Jesus returning during the Spanish Inquisition, Brook's minimalist staging of the Inquisitor's monologue is no less than a naked inquisition of our age and our answers to his questions.

The Heathersby House is a beautiful museum in the heart of Boston that features a priceless heirloom art collection. Unfortunately the museum is only famous for one thing: theft. Twelve years ago thieves made off with $20 million in paintings. Now three down-on-their-luck friends see opportunity where others see only empty frames. If someone else could steal paintings, why couldn't a trio of bumbling idiots make off with some artistic loot too? In this world premiering comedy, everyone comes for the art, but they stay for the heist.

The Public Theater's new Tony®-winning production of Hair, directed by Diane Paulus is the most electric celebration on Broadway! This exuberant musical about a group of young Americans searching for peace and love in a turbulent time has struck a resonant chord with audiences young and old. Hair features an extraordinary cast and dozens of unforgettable songs, including "Aquarius," "Let the Sun Shine In," "Good Morning, Starshine" and "Easy To Be Hard." Its relevance is undeniable. Its energy is unbridled. Its truth is unwavering. It's Hair, and it's time. While many find this show suitable for young adults (13 and older), parental discretion is advised. There is a dimly lit 20-second scene with nudity that is non-sexual in nature.

Actors Shakespeare Project presents The Hotel Nepenthe, by John Kuntz, directed by David R. Gammons.    On a cold winter night, somewhere in America, the lives of 17 people collide as they plunge into a dark, indifferent city: the scheming wife of a Senator, a hapless lover, a mother searching for her child, a bellhop with a mysterious hatbox, a sociopathic cab driver, a woman dressed in purple who may or may not travel through time, a brother and a sister confronting their grief, a self-absorbed starlet, an ordinary woman with butterfly wings. They all have one thing in common: The Hotel Nepenthe.
theater: Actors Shakespeare Project at The Storefront on Elm

sSynopsis: THE SHOWGIRL RETURNS!  This tour promises to be an absolute landmark in the career of Kylie Minogue as she intends to create a live spectacular that will surpass even her own previous groundbreaking shows. Kylie has already been working on concepts for the tour and says, "The reaction to 'Aphrodite' has been absolutely incredible and has inspired me and my creative team to develop a new show that will take all of us on a euphoric journey of joy, excitement and glamour. I can't wait to get on the road and see all my fans in 2011."

Ryan Landry and the Gold Dust Orphans present the original cast in Pussy on the House, a twisted take on Cat on a Hot Tin Roof first presented in 2004.    All the characters are back and ready to return to life! ... Brick Pollup, the tragic ex T.V. star, his gorgeous yet frustrated wife, Maggie the Cat, Big Mamma Pollup, owner of the richest polyester plantation this side a' Shanghi, who along with her lesbian lover Aunt Sukie, a whirlwind mess of tears and joy wrapped in lavender chiffon, is "only lookin' for a little peace and quiet." ... There's Mae and Gooper and Brick's ex partner, Skipper ... and you guessed it, "a whole mess a' no neck monsters".    ... But mostly there's the story. William's brilliant, heartbreaking story, (sent through The Gold Dust Orphans glitter filled strainer of course!). It's the same story of love unrequited, the same story of greed and avarice. The theme may be as old as time and yet none can deny that "Cat on a Hot Tin Roof" remains full to the brim with life's most valuable lessons. The kind hard learned by those who dwell in William's story and here ... within Big Mamma's house.  ... For this too, is a house filled to the rafters with mendacity.

Broadway's current smash hit, the internationally-acclaimed Beatles concert, RAIN -  A Tribute To The Beatles, makes its debut at the Citi Performing Arts Center Wang Theatre Friday, February 25 through Saturday, February 26. RAIN, Broadway's newest hit, comes to Boston for 3 performances only!     RAIN boasts a repertoire of nearly 200 Beatlemaniac favorites, ranging from such beloved songs as "Yesterday" and "Hey Jude" to classic hits including "Revolution" and "Come Together."     As "the next best thing to seeing The Beatles!" (Associated Press), RAIN performs the full range of The Beatles' discography live onstage, including the most complex and challenging songs that The Beatles themselves recorded in the studio but never performed for an audience.   Together longer than The Beatles, RAIN has mastered every song, gesture and nuance of the legendary foursome, delivering a totally live, note-for-note performance that's as infectious as it is transporting. From the early hits to later classics (I Want To Hold Your Hand, Hard Day's Night, Sgt. Pepper's Lonely Hearts Club Band, Let It Be, Come Together, Hey Jude and more), this adoring tribute will take you back to a time when all you needed was love, and a little help from your friends!
showName: RAIN -  A Tribute To The Beatles
theater: Citi Performing Arts Center Wang Theatre

All the music and vocals are performed totally live! Rain - A Tribute to the Beatles covers the Fab Four from the earliest beginnings through the psychedelic late 60s and their long-haired hippie, hard-rocking rooftop days.    Sing along with your family and friends to such Beatlemaniac favorites as "Let It Be," "Hey Jude," "While My Guitar Gently Weeps," "Come Together" and "Can't Buy Me Love."
showName: Rain - A Tribute to the Beatles
theater: Citi Performing Arts Center Wang Theatre

sSynopsis: Are an aging widow's bizarre sculptures evidence of creativity or insanity?    The Boston Center for American Performance (BCAP) continues its third season with Athol Fugard's The Road to Mecca, at the Boston University Theatre, Lane-Comley Studio 210.     South Africa's preeminent playwright explores the transformative power of art in this tale of an eccentric sculptor who quietly struggles against restrictive societal and religious norms.

A cherished story that has enchanted generations of readers, The Secret Garden acknowledges the fears and fancies of young people, celebrates the escapist yearnings in all of us, and, ultimately, realizes that sometimes we must leave our surroundings to find our true selves.

The first world war is over, but some battles still rage on. Elevator Repair Service (GATZ, Sound and the Fury) brings Hemmingway's novel to life on a stage littered with liquor bottles and cafe chairs, as the story winds its way through France and Spain.

Stoneham Theatre presents Sunfish, featuring music by Hyeyoung Kim, lyrics by Michael Cooper, and book by Michael Cooper and Hyeyoung Kim. Caitlin Lowans directs, with musical direction by John Howrey.    When offered a miraculous cure to restore her father's sight, a poor young girl sacrifices everything she knows and is swept up in an adventure that takes her from her small village to a fantastic undersea world. Based on a traditional Korean folk-tale.

Set in Atlanta between 1948 and 1973, Driving Miss Daisy chronicles the triumph of hope and understanding over cultural prejudice.  Daisy Werthan, a stubborn, independent Jewish widow, reluctantly surrenders the driver's seat to chauffeur Hoke Coleburn, a proud, soft-spoken black man.  With a heart-warming message of generosity and grace, the story captures the evolving relationship between the two, as Daisy comes to rely on Hoke not only as an employee, but as a valued friend.

sSynopsis: - All Ages Show -  Part of the "Backstage Pass" series, "Live at the Strand Theater" kicks off featuring the finest in local, regional, and national talent broadcast live over Penguin Radio! Seating is very limited. Order your tickets today!    Presented by Indigo Planet Records and Penguin Radio     Featuring  Ducarriganigan (Brooklyn, NY) -   Aaron Dugan (Matisyahu) and Amy Carrigan  Rachel Zamstein (NYC)  Anjelia Pelay (Asbury Park)     Aaron Dugan is a founding member and guitarist of Grammy-nominated rock/reggae band Matisyahu. He performed on all of Matisyahu's albums including 2010's "Light" and "Live at Stubbs." He plays in drummer Mark Guiliana's band Beat Music. He was a member of the dub band "Roots Tonic" (Matisyahu's backing band during live shows and recording). He also tours regularly and records with singer/songwriter Trevor Hall. He has a solo album "Theory of Everything" released on Jungulous in 2010. Aaron can be seen regularly around New York City playing improvised music with various ensembles. He has also recorded or performed with Jaymay, Maya Dunietz, Reid Taylor, Tim Lefebvre, Bill Laswell, Josh Werner, Dub Trio, Meshell Ndegeocello, Jeff Arnal, John Zorn, Roots Tonic, Bootsy Collins, Nigel Sifantus, Anders Nilsson, Madhu Siddappa, Chris Tunkel, Jason Fraticelli and many others.     Amy Carrigan is a theater maker, puppeteer, photographer and singer of music from folk and avant garde improvisational music to classical and jazz. For the past 10 years, Amy has been a core member of the Brooklyn-based puppetry company, Drama of Works, as well as a principal artist in the New York/London-based vocal and movement-based performance group, Experience Vocal Dance Company since 2005. She is the great granddaughter of Armenian Composer, Grikor Mirzaian Suni, and has an innate thirst for traditional music from around the world.    From an early age, she dedicated herself to become the world's most renowned pastry chef. Her dreams cut to black, however, following a perfect pastry storm of a faulty oven, undercooked dough and a serious bout of salmonella that landed her and four of her friends in the hospital. The young Zamstein was crushed and subsequently withdrew into silence for a period of two years, but during that time, devoured short stories and novels and poetry. She would lie on her bedroom floor for endless hours with her headphones on, soaking up every musical note, every lyrical phrase of albums by Nirvana, the Rolling Stones, Ella Fitzgerald, Led Zeppelin, the Beatles, Paul Simon and Joni Mitchell. When she finally did break her silence at the age of ten, it was only fitting that it was in song. Throughout her silent period, she had written six songs and decided to reintroduce herself by performing a small living room concert for her family and friends. And she never looked back. Like the finest pastry chef, Zamstein is never content with a single recipe; she is constantly evolving and offering new flavors for her growing fanbase to devour. While her songwriting remains fresh and unique, her sound now mixes a country roots vibe with a harder-edged rock sound more fitting of Ms. Zamstein's loveable, yet fiery personality. She is currently in the process of forming a new band, called Bird Mad Girl.    Welcome back, Rachel! One of the most popular Shore performers of the last decade and multiple Asbury Music Award nominee, Rachel returns to the Jersey Shore for a very special performance!    Anjelia Pelay, was born and raised in Toms River, N.J. It all started at the age of 5, playing Mozart and Beethoven pieces on the piano by memory. She then grew up entertaining and performing for almost her whole life. After spending some years as an actress appearing in small guest star roles in Film/Television, dappling in some dance gigs and off-broadway roles as well; Anjelia was quietly writing her original music, working hard at perfecting her craft. You may have seen her before 'in character', but her music will surprise you even more.    In her first Strand appearance, Anjelia will show everyone why she is one of the breakout Shore performers of 2011!

This discussion plays a vital role in the development of the play and helps the playwright understand if the audience fully captures the author's intentions. Lennon Perricone, the first play read by Playwrights on the Rise, has been purchased by a theater company in the mid-west and is currently being staged.

sSynopsis: Originally starring Alec Baldwin and Mary Louise Parker, this seemingly straightforward love story has an extraordinary twist. As noted in The New York Times: "Prelude to a Kiss takes a most familiar genre, romantic comedy, in directions that are idiosyncratic and challenging." Here's what happens. At the wedding of Peter and Rita, a young couple who are crazy about one another, the bride is kissed by an old man whom nobody knows. It's not until the newlyweds are on their honeymoon that Peter becomes aware that something is amiss. He gradually realizes that the disturbing change in Rita's personality is a result of the unknown man's kiss. Peter also realizes that there is only a limited time to find the elderly man and undo the damage to Rita and to their marriage.     For groups 10+, please call 201-692-0200.

Due to popular demand, The Theater Company presents once again the cult classic The Rocky Horror Show. Presented 6 years ago, our new version is fresh and not based on the movie or past production, but based on the original script with new arrangements. Rocky Horror fans will cheer, and "virgins" will become fans!
showName: Richard O'Brien's The Rocky Horror Show

sSynopsis: Featuring the characters Atticus Finch, Scout, and Boo Radley who have become iconic figures in the American consciousness and conscience, this Pulitzer-prize winning tale is considered to be one of the most important novels of the 20th century.  The production will feature an extended six-week run in anticipation of unprecedented student and audience demand.

sSynopsis: The Alvin Ailey American Dance Theater grew from the now fabled performance in March 1958, at the 92nd Street Young Men's Hebrew Association in New York. Led by Alvin Ailey and a group of young African-American modern dancers, that performance changed forever the perception of American dance. Today, led by Artistic Director Judith Jamison, AAADT has gone on to perform for an estimated 23 million people in 48 states and in 71 countries on six continents, including two historic residencies in South Africa. The company has earned a reputation as one of the most acclaimed international ambassadors of American culture, promoting the uniqueness of the African-American cultural experience and the preservation and enrichment of the American modern dance.
sTheaterAddress: Michigan State University, East Lansing, MI 48821

sSynopsis: Anne of Green Gables is in love. Pontiac Theatre IV presents the continuing story of Anne Shirley and Gilbert Blythe. This new Canadaian Musical is making its United States premiere in Pontiac. Music for Anne & Gilbert features music and lyrics by Bob Johnston and Nancy White and book/lyrics by Jeff Hochhauser adapted from the books by LM Montgomery Anne of Avonlea and Anne of the Island. "The show has charm in abundance."-Richard Ouzounian, The Toronto Star.

Meet Ferdinand the Bull, an unusual bull who prefers picking flowers to joining the bullfighters in the ring, and Danilo, a young nobleman whose father Duque Dodo has big dreams for him. Watch what happens when Danilo, the reluctant matador, meets Ferdinand in the bullring. You'll cheer for them as they refuse to go along with the crowd and strike a blow for individuality and celebrating our differences. This musical integrates Spanish, flamenco dancing and original music to create a memorable theatrical experience perfect for young audiences and their families.    Age Rating: Ages 3 to 10
sTheaterAddress: Michigan State University, East Lansing, MI 48821

sSynopsis: Secrets Untold is a drama filled romantic comedy with a twist. Three sisters living three separate lives who all have a story to tell. Stories of jealousy, envy, lies, deceit, and revenge, wrapped up into one explosive event that unravels the entire family structure. You do not want to miss these untold secrets unfold!

Combine a fun and excitement-filled evening of dining and suspense while you attempt to solve a murder case. Adventurous Denver theatergoers are brought to the Adams Mystery Playhouse, Colorado's only theater specializing in interactive dinner mysteries.

A perverse romantic comedy for the politically astute and pissed off. Billed as a sexy, political, romantic comedy the Motley Players take wide aim at the long list of public figures including, Tom and Jaquie Tancredo, Gayle and Ted Haggert, Julian Assange, Mary Cheney, Linda Chavez, Rush Limbaugh, Christine O'Donnel, Glen Beck and the whole Palin crew.

Arsenic and Old Lace, the classic Joseph Kesseling play, features an author and raving bachelor, Mortimer Brewster, who goes against his own advice and marries.  He gets into a sticky situation when he takes his new bride to visit his sweet old aunts.  He is shocked to learn that the kind old spinsters have a favorite pastime of luring gentlemen to the house only to serve them a concoction of elderberry wine with a touch of arsenic! Jerry Schell directs.

Alan Strang, a young man of seventeen, has committed a brutal act against six horses; his brilliant psychiatrist (Dr. Dysart) works to unravel the motivation behind this violent act.  Dysart applies God like skills in his attempt to fix this broken young boy, and as he does, he begins to envy the boys passion.

'Bull' McCabe is a tenant farmer with an obsession with the field he has been renting from a poor widow. After years of backbreaking toil, McCabe has transformed the field from three acres of rocky wasteland into a lush green pasture. But when the widow decides to put the property up for auction an outraged McCabe is determined to buy it at all costs.

Elwood P. Dowd is an average mild-mannered man with one slight eccentricity: he keeps introducing people to his best friend, an invisible six-and-a-half foot tall white rabbit named Harvey!  Elwood's sister Veta Louise decides to have Elwood committed to the local sanitarium, and soon the search is on for Elwood and his invisible companion.
theater: John Hand Theater, CFU's Lowry Campus

sSynopsis: Madcap Theater is a completely unscripted, interactive and award winning comedy show. Voted "Best Live Comedy" three years running, Madcap's improv show utilizes audience participation to build it's performance around, guaranteeing each show at Madcap is a totally unique and interactive experience for the audience. Above all, Madcap's standard of suitable material insures that every performance is appropriate for all types of audiences. The combination of award winning comedy and suitable material has made Madcap a destination location for family gatherings, church outings, company events and date nights.

Two arch rivals on the TV food network find themselves improbably teamed up on the same cooking show.  What happens when the two women attempt to cohost in front of a live "studio audience"? Let's just say there's double double toil and trouble that conjures up a wildly funny show with laughs galore.

Machines Like Us is made up of two alternating productions - the world premiere of Getting Betta, a touching full-length comedy by TCL playwright in residence Don Fried; and Robots Like Us, six wild, funny short plays commissioned by TCL for the festival.

ArtsPower's "Madeline and the Bad Hat," an original musical based on the much-loved book, captures the blithe yet touching spirit of Ludwig Bemelmans's "Madeline" series. It traces the adventures of a young Parisian girl who - despite starting off on the wrong foot with a mischievous new neighbor -  learns that first impressions aren't everything.
showName: Madeline and the Bad Hat - an original musical

sSynopsis: The circus comes to town in this collision-course immigration tale of a Bulgarian ringmaster, a Liberian home care worker and an Indian call center escapee.
showName: Agnes Under the Big Top, a tall tale

sSynopsis: We've all felt like we didn't fit in, whether we grew up in our hometown or moved to a new country when we were 6. For Aamera Siddiqui, growing up as an immigrant in the United States was a balancing act between her Indian heritage and her American surroundings. Aamera's world consisted of one country inside the four walls of her family's home and another country outside those walls. Curried peas and hot dogs, Catholic school uniforms and colorful saris, Urdu and English all blended and bounced off one another to shape Aamera's identity.    Told with honesty and humor, writer/performer Aamera Siddiqui's American as Curry Pie is one woman's story about immigration, assimilation, and discovering what it means to be an American. Meena Natarajan and Suzy Messerole direct.
sTheaterAddress: 30 East Tenth Street, St. Paul, MN 55101

sSynopsis: The Playwright Theatre presents Party of 1, by Morris Bobrow, directed by Brian Thompson with musical direction by Glen Dennis. This comic musical revue is about the joyful neurosis of single life. Featuring the vocal talents of Chris Bogert, Kevin Brown, Megan Van De Hay and Tara Szabo.

An American classic, Arsenic and Old Lace is nothing short of a perfectly written farcical black comedy. Spinster sisters Abby and Martha Brewster are devoted to charity and family. But the sisters have taken on another project as well - befriending lonely older gentlemen and then poisoning them with arsenic-laced elderberry wine.
After a six-year Broadway run, worldwide tours and a year in Las Vegas, the irreverent and hilarious people-and-puppet musical comedy takes on a whole new vantage in Mixed Blood's intimate theater.

When a postulant proves too high-spirited for the religious life, she is dispatched to serve as governess for the seven children of a widowed naval captain. This classic includes favorites "Do-Re-Mi," "My Favorite Things," "Sixteen Going on Seventeen," "Edelweiss," and more.
The Avenue Theater re-opens with the smash hit comedy Sylvia, by A. R. Gurney.

A mother from New Jersey roams the hills of Lockerbie Scotland, looking for her son's remains that were lost in the crash of Pan Am 103.   A poetic drama about the triumph of love over hate.   Talk back with the cast after each performance.

Get Up Your Irish: A Celebration in Music & Dance is created by Norah Rendell and Natalie O'Shea.    Echoes of issues that immigrants face today are found in this sotry of the immigrant experience from 100 years ago. The music & dance of Ireland tell the story of Irish immigration to Minnesota.    Get Up Your Irish is the story of a young boy's journey from Ireland to a new home in Saint Paul. Painted with the stereotype of the combative Irishman, this young hero finds the courage to face conflicts wiht his fists down, and to unite his community. Packed with toe-tapping dance numbers accompanied by fiddle, flute and guitar, this show will have you singing for days!    Featuring members of the Two Tap Trio with youth performers from O'Shea Irish Dance and the Center for Irish Music.
sTheaterAddress: 55 Victoria Street North, St. Paul, MN 55104

sSynopsis: Curious Theatre Company concludes its highly successful 2003-4 Season with the Regional Premiere of the searing intra-racial drama Yellowman by Dael Orlandersmith. This riveting two-actor drama was a finalist for the 2002 Pulitzer Prize, and was named as one of the ten "Best Plays of 2002-3" by the American Theatre Critics/Steinberg New Play Awards and Citations competition.  Alma, a dark-skinned black woman, and Eugene, a light-skinned black man, grow up together yearning to escape the American South. When their friendship turns to love, the different colors of their skin raise obstacles that become insurmountable. The play examines how the sins of the past become the legacy of the future and the harsh realities of internal racism, exploring the complexities of love, race, and geography.

HAIR: The American Tribal Love-Rock Musical, the 2009 Tony Award-winning musical revival, features a score including such groundbreaking numbers as "Let the Sun Shine In," Aquarius," "Hair" and "Good Morning Starshine."    The musical depicts the birth of a cultural movement in the '60s and '70s that changed America forever. It follows a group of hopeful, free-spirited young people who advocate a lifestyle of pacifism and free-love in a society riddled with intolerance and brutality during the Vietnam War. As they explore sexual identity, challenge racism, experiment with drugs and burn draft cards, the show resonates with an irresistible message of hope more than 40 years after it first opened on Broadway.     HAIR won the 2009 Tony Award for Best Musical Revival as well as the Drama Desk, Drama League, and Outer Critics Circle award for Outstanding Revival of a Musical. The production was also nominated for an additional seven Tony Awards including Best Direction, Best Choreography, Best Costume Design, Best Lighting Design and Best Sound Design. The cast recording was also nominated for a Grammy Award for Best Musical Show Album.     Directed by Diane Paulus and choreographed by Karole Armitage, HAIR features a book and lyrics by Gerome Ragni and James Rado and music by Galt MacDermot.
showName: HAIR: The American Tribal Love-Rock Musical

sSynopsis: The Guthrie Theater presents a Flying Foot Forum production of Heaven, directed by Joe Chvala.    Heaven is a mind-bending dance theater epic that follows an American war photographer on an odyssey through war-torn Bosnia in the early 1990's. Set to a hard-driving Balkan score, the dance and music fly through the realms of pop, rap, rock, percussion, and opera mixed with traditional and contemporary Balkan styles. The story is heart-wrenching and suspenseful, but surprisingly hopeful. It blasts off at the frenetic pace of a battle, stopping along the way to look at the humanity behind the suffering. It is a story of survival, hope, understanding, forgiveness and even beauty in the face some of the most horrific events the late 20th century has seen.

H.M.S. Pinafore, Gilbert and Sullivan's first major success, provides a farcical look at the mixing of social classes and the failure of idealistic socialism when put into practice. With a plot imbued with mirth and silliness, a surprise disclosure changes relationships dramatically near the end of the story. But fear not: it all works out in the end.

Every month, Sample Night Live offers about a dozen ten-minute acts consisting of a smorgasbord of G-Rated family friendly entertainment in Act I and unrated art in Act II. Performances are the first Wednesday of every month at Bryant Lake Bowl in Minneapolis.

"Gone to Greece--back in two weeks!"  Shirley Valentine's world is one of kitchens, cooking and faded dreams. At the age of 42, Shirley feels that her marriage and life are in a rut.  She longs to "drink a glass of wine in the country where grapes are grown", but when a friend invites her on holiday to Greece will Shirley have the courage to swap housework and drudgery for two weeks in the sun?     Bain Boehlke directs Cheryl Willis in Willy Russell's comedy about breaking free, living life and starting over.

Max, a musically gifted high school student, is falling off the edge of the world--and his biology teacher is the only one who's noticed. A new play about the science of life and loss, the relationships between fathers and sons, Cambodian fields, Bolivian rainforests and redemption, Song of Extinction won the 2009 Harold and Mimi Steinberg/ATCA New Play Award (given by the American Theater Critics Association), the 2008 Ted Schmitt Award for Outstanding New Play by the Los Angeles Drama Critics Circle and the 2008 LA Weekly's Production of the Year.

The Great American History Theatre presents A Tale of Twin Cities, written and performed by Kevin Klingm with music by Simone Perrin. Suzy Messerole directs.    Beloved Minnesota storyteller Kevin Kling teams up with the lovely and talented Simone Perrin to spin some yarns and sing some tunes exploring the sometimes loving, sometimes tumultuous, often hysterical shared histories of our sibling cities: Minneapolis and St. Paul. From their beginnings as St. Anthony and Pigs Eye through their growth as the milling and commerce centers of the Midwest, these "twins" have shared a lot of adventures over the years.
sTheaterAddress: 30 East Tenth Street, St. Paul, MN 55101

sSynopsis: The summer of 1935 is a hot one in Maycomb, Alabama. Eight-year-old Scout watches her father stand against the town's anger when he defends a young black man accused of raping a white woman. Scout and her community come of age together, helping us connect with our own high ideals.    Christopher Sergel's stage adaptation of Harper Lee's To Kill a Mockingbird is directed by David Mann.

This play by John Cariani is a whimsical look at the joys and perils of romance. Magical happenings bloom beneath the snow drifts in the remote, mythical town of Almost, Maine. On a cold, clear, moonless night in the middle of winter, all is not what it seems.  Beneath the glow of the northern lights in a star-filled sky the residents of Almost, a town that is almost a town, find themselves falling in and out of love in surprising and often hilarious ways.  Hearts are broken and knees are bruised, but the hearts mend and the bruises heal -almost- in this delightful midwinter night's dream. Don't miss these nine tales of love in the time of frostbite - tales that aim for the heart by way of the funny bone.

Who doesn't remember the board game Clue, Miss Scarlet, Professor Plum, Colonel Mustard and the rest of the crowd? Was it the lead pipe, or the revolver? Did it happen in the kitchen or in the billiard room?  Not often does a board game come to life on the stage where all of the characters sing and dance as well!  The audience assists in drawing the cards that start the game, and they play along throughout the evening, helping to solve the crime.  Critics called it, "A show for the whole family…..effervescent fun."  AND there are so many possible endings that no two performances are the same, so you can see this one more than once!

A rare combination of unprecedented originality and blinding talent, The Drowsy Chaperone boldly addresses a great unspoken desire in all of our hearts: to be entertained. If you've ever sat in a dark theatre and thought, "Dear Lord in heaven, please let it be good," this is the show for you! It all begins when a die-hard musical-theater fan plays his favorite cast album on his turntable, and the musical literally bursts to life in his living room, telling the rambunctious tale of a brazen Broadway starlet trying to find, and keep, her true love.

In this wilder, darker continuation of the Henry IV story, anarchy looms, rebellion is reignited and loyalties turn on a dime. The antics of a more degenerate Falstaff and betrayals in court cast a shadow as the once wayward Prince Hal struggles to prove to his dying father--and himself--that he can be the ruler his country so desperately needs. Don't miss the uneasy transfer of power from father to son in a production that dynamically juxtaposes old and new.     The play contains bawdy scenes in a brothel, as well as challenging political and moral themes. It is best suited for students 13 and up who have some knowledge of the historical context.
theater: Elizabethan Stage/Allen Pavilion, Oregon Shakespeare Festival

sSynopsis: The road to Hell is paved with honorable intentions. Adoring commoners would crown Caesar, but Caesar's fellow politicians debate the popular leader's ambition. Fearful for the Republic, tormented by uncertainty and driven by questionable motives, they plot an assassination. What justifies murder, and what is the shocking aftermath? The volatile, complex nature of government and the fallibility of those in power boil down in the intimate New Theatre to one pressure cooker of a tragedy.    The play is best suited for well prepared viewers 12 and up.
theater: New Theatre at Oregon Shakespeare Festival

sSynopsis: The Duke's authoritarian deputy, Angelo, is hell-bent on stamping out moral decay. He reactivates outdated Draconian laws and aims his arrogant crosshairs at a young man whose fiancée is pregnant, sentencing him to death. Angelo is sternly incorruptible--until he meets Isabela, a beautiful religious novice whose desirability arouses him. Flavored with live music by the mariachi band Las Colibri, Rauch's vigorous, modern production of Shakespeare's tragicomedy reveals what can happen when sex, religion and politics collide.    Shakespeare's tragicomedy explores restraint and lack of restraint. It is a compelling mix of the things we're still obsessed with--morality, religion and politics. It is best suited for mature 14-year-olds and up. Prologue recommended. Please view our full age recommendation here.    Schedule Varies, see website.

Neil Simon's side-splitting comedy, is the story of four couples who arrive at the house of New York City's deputy mayor to celebrate his wedding anniversary.  However, the party never begins because the host has shot himself and his wife is missing.  The first couple to arrive, after seeing what has happened (it is just a flesh wound), try to cover up the situation to avoid a scandal.  The cover up becomes increasingly difficult to sustain as more guests arrive and nobody can keep track of who has been told what! Hilarity abounds as doors slam and the situation spins wildly out of control!  The arrival of two policemen at the height of the confusion prompts one of the funniest finales Simon has ever written.
Theatresports is a wildly fun improv competition in which two squads of performers create spontaneous scenes from audience suggestions which are then scored by a panel of judges.

Feel your body move and your spirit soar as the master drummers and dancers of Djembe Fire! take you on a rhythmic journey across Africa. Authentic instruments, costumes, stories and songs come together in this unique performance that will delight young and old alike. Audiences join in the show, adding their energy to that of the talented performers and making each Djembe Fire! performance a truly unique experience.    For ages 3+
From basement Blues to Broadway's Black musicals to R&B and Jazz, this fast paced, jumping musical revue is the doctor's entertainment prescription if you want to feel good!
sTheaterAddress:
Dallas Convention Center, 605 South Griffin
Dallas, TX 75202
theater: Black Academy of Arts and Letters

sSynopsis: Collin Cabaret: Changing Lives, Collin College's college's signature fundraising event, seeks to raise money for student scholarships by showcasing the artistic talents of Collin College students, alumni and faculty. Guests are treated to live performances featuring music, song, dance and theater.
theater: Eisemann Center for The Performing Arts

sSynopsis: Cornelia Wellington Heister and her sister, Dorthea, are wealthy orphans whose only living relatives are a hillbilly family who run a general store in Lone Mule, Tennessee. Their father's will insists that the girls spend their summers in Lone Mule with their Uncle Cyrus Goolus or forfeit their share of the fortune. Cornelia in particular hates the arrangement, and Uncle Cyrus is a miser who sees a chance to make himself some money. He decides to make life miserable for the girls so they'll run away -- and he will inherit the entire fortune himself. In an avalanche of fun and laughter, he shows the girls the absolute worst of hillbilly living. They don't discourage easily, however, and Cornelia even finds herself the object of adoration of Slim Hawkenshaw and begins to realize that perhaps mountaineers are human beings after all. Luckily, Cornelia finds out about her Uncle's scam and decides two can play at that game! She and Dot pretend to go all out for the hillbilly life and even show Uncle Cyrus a thing or two.
theater: Fitzpatrick Auditorium at Kernersville Elementary School

sSynopsis: Texas playwright Horton Foote has delighted us with dozens of classic plays (The Trip to Bountiful) and films (To Kill a Mockingbird, Tender Mercies). In an unprecedented collaboration, Dallas Theater Center brings together theaters and institutions across the metroplex for the region-wide Foote Festival to celebrate the work of the legendary "quiet voice of Texas." As part of this history-making festival, Dallas Theater Center presents the regional premiere of this richly drawn character study of a multi-generational Texas family during the 1980s oil bust. A hit on Broadway last year, Dividing the Estate is a clear-eyed, witty portrayal of a family slow to surrender its sense of entitlement--and quick to start a feeding frenzy when the matriarch passes on.
theater: Dee and Charles Wyly Theatre  The AT&T Performing Arts Center

sSynopsis: A wickedly funny comedy from the writer of American Beauty and creator/producer of the HBO series' Six Feet Under and True Blood, Five Women Wearing the Same Dress tells the story of five reluctant, identically clad bridesmaids hiding out in an upstairs bedroom to avoid the proceedings of an ostentatious wedding reception at a Knoxville, Tennessee, estate. As the afternoon wears on, these five very different women joyously discover a common bond in this comical, irreverent and touching celebration of the women's spirit.
showName: Five Women Wearing the Same Dress

sSynopsis: Kathy Burks & Company bring their clever twist to this familiar fairy tale in a sophisticated and witty musical version that will have you looking for a frog to kiss! We they live happily ever after? We won't tell. But the ending will have you jumping!
theater: Dallas Children's Theater, Rosewood Center for Family Arts

sSynopsis: With language used like a loaded weapon, Naomi Iizuka's splendidly realized drama about a small town tragedy of working-class people is an eerie and powerful narration; a kind of ghost story set in the cave country of North Carolina. The disappearance of a young girl lost in the cave at the edge of town gathers the community to puzzle out the meaning and the circumstances of the mysterious loss.

Beloved storyteller and illustrator Steven Kellogg re-imagines this familiar folktale to create a friendly, colorful and joyful story. A simple elf and his mysterious pipe frees a town of its rats and transforms its inhabitants with the happiest of endings!
theater: Dallas Children's Theater, Rosewood Center for Family Arts

sSynopsis: They keep coming - poet after poet - ripping, rapping and rhyming to a melodious evening of captivating music and spoken word. It's the Dallas/Fort Worth metropolitan area's best of the best poets!
sTheaterAddress:
Dallas Convention Center, 605 South Griffin
Dallas, TX 75202
theater: Black Academy of Arts and Letters

sSynopsis: Part of the citywide Harold Foote Festival.  Foote was the master of the one-act, and in the 50's and 60's made regular contributions of Texas stories in the format which were always enthusiastically reviewed and enjoyed in New York. In 1982, he wrote The Roads to Home, which is a set of three one-acts written to be performed together in one performance, and centered on three women whose small Texas town's values ill-equip them for the tough city lives they are now leading. Foote's masterful storytelling is full of unblinking honesty and laced with humor. In The Roads to Home, he reveals that the women's small town ways, built on kindness and discretion, have no system for dealing with less well-behaved feelings like terror, anguish, and passion that loom in their big city lives.
sTheaterAddress:
2800 Routh Street, The Quadrangle at Howell
Dallas, TX 75201

sSynopsis: In 1980, Andy Warhol - he of the 15 minutes of fame and the giant soup cans - opened an exhibit of 10 silk-screen portraits of famous Jews. They were not, shall we say, well received.    They were the target of scorn by many art critics and praise by the public who understood and appreciated them. Thirty-one years later, comic storyteller Josh Kornbluth takes up the issue of the once controversial exhibit and what it means -- to him personally and to a community of art lovers at large and most importantly asks you...to judge for yourself.
showName: Andy Warhol: Good For The Jews?

sSynopsis: The 12th Annual Arizona Young Artists' Competition showcases the diverse talent of aspiring young Arizona performers, ages 15-18.    The top four finalists in each discipline of Acting, Dance and Voice, will compete for a $1,000 cash prize.  Prizes are awarded in each category.

A play fifty years in the making, American master Edward Albee has penned a prequel to his brilliant one-act play, The Zoo Story.    This full play is a meticulously calibrated and brutal look at the trapped lives of three human animals, each in their own zoo.  Act I opens with Peter and his wife, Ann, whose frank conversation (which begins with "We should talk.") veers off into dangerously personal territory.  It's the kind of talk that can drive a husband out for a walk - to Central Park, for Act II, where Jerry, a desperate and lonely outcast, awaits Peter.  At Home at the Zoo bares its teeth to threaten our delicately balanced world, growling at each passerby through the bars.

Prepare to leave all your preconceptions at the door...AXIS Dance Company, one of the worlds most acclaimed and innovative ensembles of performers with and without disabilities will change the way you think about dance and the possibilities of the human body forever. Founded in 1987, AXIS has become a jewel of contemporary dance and disability culture and has paved the way for physically integrated dance form. They will inspire you and show you what dance can be.

The ninth edition in the series of musical revues featuring songs from Broadway productions.    Take a musical journey with SCAN Originals as they explore the many types of jobs we do to make a living.

The Canadian Brass have brightened concert halls and festivals across the globe with their showmanship, lively banter and humorous pranks, performing everything from Vivaldi to Duke Ellington to Broadway. They may enter the theater in a New Orleans jazz funeral procession, then scamper across the stage in tutus as they perform Swan Lake.    Audiences have long delighted in their quirky sense of humor, comparing them to the Marx Brothers and the early Beatles. In four decades, this quintet has developed a reputation for its jazz/classical fusion and trademark uniforms -- tuxedos with white sneakers. They are simply the "world's leading brass ensemble". (The Washington Post)

Laugh, Have Fun and Celebrate at Arizona's ONLY Vaudeville Inspired Illusion Show!    Have a special night out with national award-winning entertainers Roland Sarlot and Susan Eyed's fun Vaudeville inspired intimate illusion show, a Tucson Treasure and Arizona Attraction!    BONUS: For those choosing to dine before or after the performance, your ticket offers a buy one dinner entrée and receive a second equal or lesser priced FREE ENTREE at either hotel restaurant.    DOUBLE BONUS: Use gift code "mania" for $5 off EVERY ticket in your order.    "Outstanding!" -Fox News   "Amazing!" -LA Weekly  "Best show in Tucson!" -Tucson Citizen    "Phenomenal!" -ABC  "Masters of the craft" -East Valley Tribune  "Delight in Sleight" -Where Magazine
showName: Carnival of Illusion - An Evening of Intimate Magical Wonders

sSynopsis: For almost twenty years Chandler Symphony Orchestra has been serving the community by offering concerts to the public, free of charge. Families discover exquisite music of exceptional quality at an unbelievable price!    Esteemed Conductor, Jack Herriman, and Associate Conductor, Alex Zheng, lead a wide range of volunteer musicians from across the Valley of the Sun, providing quality symphonic and orchestral music to delighted audiences. In keeping with the underlying premise of the Chandler Symphony, concerts are provided to the public free of charge, so that live classical music remains accessible to everyone.

The model for the hip 21st century pianist, Christopher O'Riley is a talk show host for aspiring classical musicians on NPR (From the Top) and a master of the art of reinterpreting the music of alternative rock artists for classical piano. His latest CD, Out of My Hands, includes transcriptions of songs by Tears for Fears, Tori Amos and Radiohead. A formidable pianist in his own right, O'Riley won awards at the Leeds, Van Cliburn and Busoni competitions, as well as an Avery Fisher Career Grant. The quality of both his playing and his arrangements is what distinguishes him from other crossover artists; his CD True Love Waits received the only four-star review ever given by Rolling Stone to a classical pianist. Constantly in pursuit of "inhabiting the music," O'Riley's obsessive love of musical exploration is never more evident than in live performance. He is the "modern pianistic troubadour, transmogrifying musically simple rock songs into cascading tapestries of keyboard figurations" (The Washington Post).

Life's twists don't follow a script. Welcome to Marty Kriesberg's community center acting class! In a small Vermont town, four lost individuals plunge into Marty's class, each with their own set of expectations. But are they truly ready for what her exercises may reveal about them and their classmates? Actors Theatre is thrilled to bring you the Arizona premiere of this inventive and absorbing comedy - one of this season's most talked about new plays. This funny, big-hearted tale, and winner of the 2010 OBIE Award for Best New American Play, is a potent reminder of the impact we can have on each others lives.

A Grammy Award-winning recording artist and host of NPR's popular JazzSet program, Dee Dee Bridgewater is a consummate entertainer and sparkling ambassador for jazz. As a student, she toured the Soviet Union in 1969 with the University of Illinois Big Band before making her New York debut in 1970 as vocalist for the band led by Thad Jones and Mel Lewis, one of the premier jazz orchestras of the time. In 1975, she took Broadway by storm, winning the Tony Award for her role as Glinda the Good Witch in The Wiz. This began a long line of awards and accolades as well as opportunities to work in Tokyo, Los Angeles, Paris and London, where she garnered the coveted Laurence Olivier Award nomination as 'Best Actress' for her tour de force portrayal of jazz legend Billie Holiday in Stephen Stahl's Lady Day.    Bridgewater again channels the mystique of Lady Day in this special concert of songs made famous by Billie Holiday, which includes music from her new CD, Eleanora Fagan (1915-1959): To Billie with Love from Dee Dee. "Bridgewater is amazing, the type of performer who makes you wonder if you've ever seen or heard a better singer … she seemed to morph into Holiday." (AllAboutJazz.com)
showName: Dee Dee Bridgewater To Billie With Love: A Celebration of Lady Day

sSynopsis: Center Dance Ensemble continues their celebration of the newly renovated theater with a program featuring the first piece ever performed by CDE at the Herberger Theater -  the folk-dance opera, "The Ballad of Barbara Allen", written by Dee Strickland Johnson (Buckshot Dee), plus other works from the CDE repertoire.

Born into the household of one of the most popular singers in the world, Frank Sinatra Jr. recalls wanting to become a piano player and songwriter from his earliest days. By his early teens he was performing at local clubs and venues and at age 19 he became the vocalist for Sam Donahue's band. He also spent considerable time with Duke Ellington, learning the music business. While easily one of the best vocalists working today in his own right, it is the nostalgia for his father's immortal work that ensures that there will always be a packed house whenever Frank Sinatra Jr. takes the stage. Here he is accompanied by a 20 piece band under the musical direction of Terry Woodson.

This show skewers stereotypes, archetypes, prejudices and assumptions, both toward and within the disabled community.    Beginning with the unlikely story of the first disabled settlers at Plymouth Rock and ending with the fractured fairy tale of Cripperella.
Honk! Jr. is a contemporary retelling of Hans Christian Andersen's classic story, "The Ugly Duckling" and features a Joseph and the Amazing Technicolor Dreamcoat-like score that everyone will enjoy.
sTheaterAddress: 40404 N. Gavilan Peak Parkway, Anthem, AZ 85086

sSynopsis: International recording artist Dennis Rowland and renowned trumpeter/author Dr. Jesse McGuire lead the Extreme Decibel Big Band for an exceptional evening of music and entertainment.    Join these artists in their personal commitment to education, literacy and support of those with learning disabilities.  Enjoy an elegant hors d'oeuvres reception and silent auction, followed by a premiere concert performance in Stage West.    Arizona Literacy & Learning Center is dedicated to helping students of all ages, who struggle with reading, receive proper learning assessments and provide the interventions required to help them overcome a learning disability or reading difference.  Our goal is to help each student with a reading difference reach their learning potential, finish school and be career ready.  Last year more than 1,700 individuals benefited from ALLC's various literacy programs and we invite you to be a part of this life-changing work.    Age appropriation: 18+

Late Nite Catechism is an interactive comedy with you, the audience member, as a student in this adult catechism class. Sister reminds us of the days when the women in black constantly scolded us to keep our mouths shut, our feet on the floor, and our hands to ourselves! Join us as Sister gives her own humorous take on the Lives of the Saints, Vatican II, and growing up Catholic in America.

America fell in love with The Lennon Sisters on The Lawrence Welk show and have remained in love ever since! The Lennon Sisters charmed the nation with their sweet-voiced harmonies and natural vocal talents. This combination along with striking looks, unassuming personalities and strong family values earned them a place in the hearts of millions of fans. Their stardom has lasted almost 50 years. The Lennon Sisters are truly American legends.

Tucson: February 26 - March 19, 2011  Phoenix: March 24 - April 10, 2011     Meet the Kurnitz family. Grandma is the matriarch with a will of iron and a hardwood cane who spared no rod in raising her four children.    When her two teenage grandsons are forced by circumstances to live with her for a year, the clash of generations and battle of wills leads the whole family to learn important lessons about duty, devotion, trust and love.  Winner of the Pulitzer Prize and the Tony Award for Best Play, and as comical as it is poignant, Lost in Yonkers is the masterwork of Neil Simon's career and is certain to leave you spellbound with laughter and tears.

Andy Warhol, Sigur Ros, Roy Lichtenstein, Radiohead, Robert Rauschenberg and John Cage. These are just some of the major icons with whom Merce Cunningham collaborated in order to create his avant-garde dances inspired by anthropology, the I-Ching and Zen Buddhism. According to the wishes of the late Merce Cunningham, the legacy tour will be the last opportunity to see the iconic dance company perform before they disband.    Celebrated as Diaghilev's successor, Merce Cunningham "reinvented dance … the elegance, simplicity and force of his work are unique … he taught us something new and powerful" (Mikhail Baryshnikov). "Merce spent more than 50 years creating dances of relentless rigor, works so pure in concept and immaculate in execution that they can take your breath away," wrote The Times. He was American modern dance's equivalent of Nijinsky: the long neck, the animal intensity, the amazing leap". (The New York Times)

Beauty, truth, ambition and tradition. This beautiful play tells the story of a young Hassidic artist torn between his observant Jewish community and his need to create. Difficult choices between art and faith, passion and family, course through this stirring adaptation of a modern classic, bringing to life the heartbreak and triumph of what it means to be an artist.

The celebrated multiphonic singers from Tibet's Drepung Loseling Monastery return to Scottsdale to share their centuries-old sacred traditions. Robed in magnificent costumes and playing traditional Tibetan instruments -- from 10-foot long dung-chen horns to gyaling trumpets -- the Loseling monks perform ancient temple music and dances that are believed to generate energies conducive to world healing.    The music of the Drepung Loseling monks was featured on the Golden Globe-nominated soundtrack of the film Seven Years in Tibet, starring Brad Pitt, and they performed with Philip Glass at Lincoln Center in the live presentation of his award-winning score to the Martin Scorsese film Kundun. In addition to touring internationally, the monks have released several best-selling recordings and collaborated with artists as diverse as Paul Simon, Edie Brickell, Natalie Merchant, the Beastie Boys and the Grateful Dead's Mickey Hart, to name but a few.    The Mystical Arts of Tibet tour is co-produced by Richard Gere Productions and Drepung Loseling Institute, the North American seat of Drepung Loseling Monastery, India. Endorsed by His Holiness the Dalai Lama, the tour has three basic purposes: to make a contribution to world peace and healing; to generate a greater awareness of the endangered Tibetan civilization; and to raise support for the Tibetan refugee community in India.    The monks will be in residency at Scottsdale Center for the Performing Arts during the week of their performance, creating a sand mandala and presenting a variety of free lectures and discussions.
showName: The Mystical Arts of Tibet: Sacred Music Sacred Dance for World Healing

sSynopsis: A magnet for media attention, Nobuyuki Tsujii achieved a superhuman victory when he tied for the gold medal with Haochen Zhang in the most recent Van Cliburn International Piano Competition. The first Japanese and the first blind pianist to win the coveted award, Tsujii is a phenomenon on the classical music scene. Already the subject of a documentary and a mega star in Japan, he inspired Time Magazine to coin the phrase "Nobu Fever."    With few piano scores available in Braille, Tsujii learns the music by ear as he listens to custom-made recordings that are broken down into the left hand and right hand parts. Tsujii's meeting of the legendary R&B singer Stevie Wonder was "the happiest moment of my life," according to Tsujii. Perhaps it was Stevie Wonders' as well.    Program:  Mozart: Sonata in C Major, K. 330  Beethoven: Sonata No. 17 in D Minor, Op. 31, No. 2, Tempest  Mussorgsky: Pictures at an Exhibition

Founded in 1970 by Joan Myers Brown, the Philadelphia Dance Company, affectionately known as Philadanco, has danced its way into the hearts of America. Created out of a need to provide opportunities for Black dancers, who were then systematically denied entrance in many local dance schools, Philadanco has since grown into a professional dance company that is recognized across the nation and around the world for its artistic integrity, superbly trained dancers and electrifying performances. Philadanco easily moves from the classical music of Mahler, Bach and Ravel to the modern rhythms of Prince, Wumni Olaiya and Earth Wind and Fire. A resident dance company of the Kimmel Center for the Performing Arts since 2000, Philadanco has performed throughout the United States, Europe, Asia, United Kingdom and the Caribbean and with major orchestras.    In celebration of Philadanco's 40th-anniversary season, a number of new works have been commissioned for the company, including one by Jawole Willa Jo Zollar, founder and artistic director of the Urban Bush Women, whose imaginative choreography is well-known to Scottsdale audiences. "(Philadanco) can do just about anything: leap like arrows in flight, spin, stretch, kick and melt like hot wax." (The Washington Post)

Praised by the Village Voice for its "eye-popping effects, excellent showbiz-savvy performers" and "lusty sensual movement," the rock opera Remember Me is a spectacular collaboration between Parsons Dance Company and the East Village Opera Company. This modern re-telling of a tragic love triangle dazzles with lighting, sets, costumes, multimedia effects, dancers and singers that find company founder David Parsons "entering the realm of pop spectacle with a vengeance." (Village Voice)    If you prefer Queen to Puccini, then Remember Me is for you, touching lightly on opera's most popular vocal moments -- including arias from La Bohème, Carmen, Rigoletto and Turandot. And all the most lurid aspects of opera are here -- romance, seduction, revenge and tragic love - placed within the context of Parsons' sexily exuberant dancers.    The "rockra" promises a splendid encore: the company's greatest hit, Caught. Gravity-defying dance interacts with strobe lights effects in this triumphant tour-de-force.

Sometimes in life, things come full circle. That's the story of Ricky Skaggs. By age 21, he was already considered a "recognized master" of one of America's most demanding art forms, but his career took him in other directions, catapulting him to popularity and success in the mainstream of country music. Now the road has brought him back to where it all began - bluegrass music. With eight consecutive Grammy-nominated classics behind him the bluegrass music genre is undoubtedly in good hands with the masterful Skaggs at the helm.

America's favorite cowboys, Riders in the Sky are truly exceptional! For thirty years these Grammy Award winners have been reviving and revitalizing the Comedy & Western genre with their own legendary wacky humor and way-out Western wit, and all along encouraging buckaroos and buckarettes to live life "The Cowboy Way!" They were the first exclusively western music artists to join the Grand Ol' Opry Radio Show. Riders performed "Woody's Round Up" in "Toy Story 2," with the album of the same name, garnering Riders their first Grammy Award in 2001 for "Best Musical Album for Children." Two years later, Riders roped their second Grammy in the same category, for "Monsters Inc.

The timeless trouble-maker Aladdin is up to his old tricks in James Norris's adaption of the classic tale from The Book of One Thousand and One Nights.    Written long before Disney's feature film saw its debut, Norris's adaption is an opportunity for children to see their favorite hero Aladdin in a story honoring the original tale.    Aladdin and the Wonderful Lamp lets children delight in the possibilities of a wish-granting genie, but--as "wonderful" as Aladdin's lamp seems to be--we must always learn to be careful what we wish for...because it might come true!

Cinderella is forced to live with her cold hearted stepmother and homely stepsisters. Every young maiden in the kingdom is invited to a Royal Ball so the Crown Prince can find a bride. Cinderella's stepmother and stepsisters go to the ball, leaving her behind. When she is visited by her fairy godmother, all her wishes come true.

New York's #1 Interactive show, The Awesome 80s Prom, is now in Boston! The Awesome 80s Prom is a blast-from-the-past party in the style of Tony 'n Tina's Wedding and The Donkey Show set at Wanaget High's Senior Prom... in 1989!    All your favorite characters from your favorite '80s movies are at THE PROM, from the Captain of the Football Team to the Asian Exchange Student, from the Geek to the hottie Head Cheerleader, and they're all competing for Prom King and Queen. And just like on "American Idol", the audience decides who wins, all while moonwalking to retro hits like "Girls Just Wanna Have Fun" and "Wake Me Up Before You Go Go!"    Come "Back In Time", to quote a Huey Lewis tune, and join the breakdance circle or just sit back and watch the '80s drama unfold.    Come on, you know you have a Members Only jacket somewhere... and if you're lucky, you'll even get to dance with The Captain of the Football Team.    Ticket Information    Prom Committee - $39.99: Admission to the Prom  Prom Prince/Princess - $65.00: Admission to the Prom, Wanaget High T-Shirt, Goodie bag  Cool Kids Table - $49.99: Booth reserved on dance floor (for groups up to 10 people)  Year Book Committee - $99.99: Booth reserved by main bar (seats up to 20 people)

Seussical The Musical is a family musical based on the books of Dr. Seuss. You'll see some of Dr. Seuss' favorite characters such as The Cat in the Hat, Horton the Elephant, Jojo, Gertrude McFuzz and Mayzie La Bird.

The critically acclaimed Blue Man Group creates experiences that defy categorization. Blue Man Group is best known for their theatrical  performances that feature three bald and blue characters who take the  audience through a multi-sensory, multi-media journey that combines theatre,  percussion, music, art, science, and vaudeville into a form of entertainment  that is like nothing else. People from all over the world, from all walks of  life and from all age groups have been fans of Blue Man Group!  A live band whose haunting tribal rhythms help drive the show to its  unforgettable climax accompanies Blue Man Group!

Tucson: March 23 - 27, 2011  Phoenix: March 10 - 20, 2011     Hide the kiddies, cage the pets and stock up on the laughing gas... they're back!    Last season The Second City had Arizonans laughing so hard at ourselves we were gasping for breath (...or was that an ozone alert?), falling out of our chairs (...or were those the monsoon winds?) and splitting our sides (...or were we just left out in the sun too long?).     From the comedy empire that gave us such comedy giants as Tina Fey, Steve Carell, Stephen Colbert, Bill Murray, John Belushi, Gilda Radner and a whole slew of others, comes a new romp about the search for love in the digital age.  Whether you've been poked, winked or tweeted-- or even found love the (gasp!) old-fashioned way-- you'll LOL at this hilarious look at the technology that was supposed to make our love lives so much easier, but only made it that much more complicated.  This new comedy also includes some of the Second City trademark improvisation and audience interaction that is guaranteed to make you smile.  Featuring a virtual appearance by Fred Willard!
showName: Sex and The Second City: Version 2.0
theater: Arizona Theatre Company, Herberger Theater Center

sSynopsis: It's Saturday nights and Reverend Oglethorpe has invited the Sanders Family Singers to provide an uplifting evening of singing', clappin' and hilarious stories. The gospel tunes include Church in the Wildwood, Rock of Ages, Whispering Hope and I'll Fly Away.

Rodgers and Hammerstein's immortal musical has touched the hearts of audiences around the world. Set against the backdrop of the Austrian Alps, The Sound of Music tells the true story of a high-spirited aspiring nun who falls in love with a widowed naval captain and his seven unruly children. The delightful and inspiring story of the Trapp Family Singers includes such memorable songs as Climb Ev'ry Mountain, My Favorite Things, Edelweiss, The Sound of Music, Do-Re-Mi and So Long Farewell.

Tuscon: January 22 - February 12    Phoenix: February 17 - March 6    In this lavish world premiere comedy, we discover what every Broadway star already knows - that the real drama on stage happens when the curtain is down. It is the late 1930s, and Alfred Lunt and Lynn Fontanne, the two most revered stars of the Broadway stage, have decided to perform Chekhov's masterpiece The Sea Gull. But first they must retreat to 'investigate' the play at Ten Chimneys, their legendary Wisconsin estate, where they are surrounded by actors, family and hangers-on. When a young actress named Uta Hagen arrives, a romantic triangle begins to mirror the events in Chekhov's play about passion and art. The result is a funny, poignant and revealing look at the private lives of great artists who never really leave the stage. Ten Chimneys is a world premiere by Jeffrey Hatcher, award-winning author of ATC's Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde, Ella and Tuesdays with Morrie.

Musical Mayhem is not your grandma's cabaret!     We are a diverse and versatile group of professional singers and comedians who will take you on a journey of everything the Great White Way has to offer!  With Then & Now, spend Act One taking a trip back in time to classic Broadway with songs from Oklahoma, West Side Story, Brigadoon, Pal Joey, Showboat and more.  Enjoy Act Two's take on modern Broadway with songs from Rent, Wicked, Phantom of the Opera, Avenue Q, The 25th Annual Putnam County Spelling Bee and much more!    Our fast paced hilarious shows are one part sarcasm, two parts NYC piano bar, blended with some light comedy improvisation, and then stirred with a splash of vodka and an olive.  Enjoy this live singing evening of phenomenal voices and hilarity more than once as our amazing rotating cast guarantees that you will never see exactly the same fabulous show twice!    Musical Mayhem Cabaret - under-rehearsed, over-dramatic, and guaranteed to leave you on the edge of your seat begging for more!    Directed by Dana Cianciotto and Erin Meyer.

The name "Winans" and gospel music are synonymous and Vickie Winans definitely lives up to her name after 25 years of continuously singing the good news of Jesus Christ. The captivating vocals of this multi-talented artist are like a soulful, fine tuned instrument that piques the emotions, and uplifts the spirit. Vickie lends a high-powered, energetic, yet smooth and inspirational style as showcased in all her Grammy-nominated, Stellar Award and NAACP Award Winning albums.

Indulge your sweet tooth for adventure with this treat of an opera. In this classic fairy tale, a walk in the forest turns into a discovery of delights and frights. A gingerbread house tempts Hansel and Gretel's taste buds, but beware! Behind those sugar-coated walls lurks a witch! Hansel and Gretel must stick together to free the forest from a wicked spell. Come see what two clever children can do!
showName: Boston Lyric Opera: Hansel and Gretel
sTicketPrice: $12.00 for kids; $18.00 for adults. Tickets available December 1.
