13 is a musical about growing up. New Yorker Evan Goldman attempts to maneuver the pressure of becoming an adult, while dealing with his parents divorce. To top it all off, he just found out he is moving to a small town in Indiana. When he gets there, all Evan wants to do is lay low, make friends and survive the school year. However, it's not as easy as it sounds. The star quarterback seems to have it out for Evan and his only friend, Patrice, won't talk to him. Recently seen on Broadway, 13 is a hilarious high-energy musical for all ages with an unforgettable rock score from Tony-Award winner Jason Robert Brown.

Inspired by interviews with German gentile women and set during and after the Third Reich, All Through the Night is a stylistic and surrealistic play that sweeps through the lives of these German women from their teen years to adulthood during the Holocaust, and the aftermath. The Nazi regime impacts the lives of these women as they struggle over work, religion, marriage, and motherhood. Faced with overwhelmingly difficult choices, the women survive or succumb to Hitler's reign--and all are changed forever.     Recommended for ages 13 and older.

It is 1979. Esme Allen is an actress in London's West End just at the moment when the West End is ceasing to offer actors a regular way of life. The visit of her young daughter, Amy, and her new boyfriend brings conflict between the two and sets in train a series of events that only find their shape eighteen years later.     Recommended for age 13 and older.

Village Theatre hits the bullseye this season with Irving Berlin's famous Broadway musical Annie Get Your Gun. This Wild West show-within-a-show tells the ageless love story of the sharpest sharpshooter Annie Oakley and Frank Butler, the heart-throb of Buffalo Bill's traveling show. Hum along to unforgettable tunes like "There's No Business Like Show Business," "I Got The Sun in the Morning," and "Anything You Can Do I Can Do Better" as we celebrate one of Broadway's most enduring triumphs on the Mainstage.
theater: Village Theatre - Francis J. Gaudette Theatre

sSynopsis: Help celebrate National Poetry Month on Bainbridge Island! Explore the musical language of poetry with Jack Prelutsky, the first U.S. Children's Poet Laureate, as he reads from his collection of wonderful, whimsical verses, plus other delightful poems.
sTheaterAddress: 200 Madison Avenue North, Bainbridge Island, WA 98110

sSynopsis: Village Theatre hits the bullseye this season with Irving Berlin's famous Broadway musical Annie Get Your Gun. This Wild West show-within-a-show tells the ageless love story of the sharpest sharpshooter Annie Oakley and Frank Butler, the heart-throb of Buffalo Bill's traveling show. Hum along to unforgettable tunes like "There's No Business Like Show Business," "I Got The Sun in the Morning," and "Anything You Can Do I Can Do Better" as we celebrate one of Broadway's most enduring triumphs on the Mainstage.
theater: Village Theatre - Francis J. Gaudette Theatre

sSynopsis: Stone Soup celebrates the XX chromosome with a resounding bang as the Annual One-Act Play Festival transforms into The Double (XX) Fest, with plays and readings written and directed exclusively by women from both the Seattle area and the rest of the US as well as a 24-Hour Play Fest and writing workshops, all taking place in both Up- and DownStage theatres on Stone Way.

A new kind of Greek Tragedy.  Where the South Side Locos are Kings and Spanglish rules.    A Chicano take on the Greek tragedy Electra, Luís Alfaro's Electricidad is a brutally modern adaptation of the classic revenge saga set within gang culture of the "barrio". One of the foremost Latino playwrights in the U.S. and winner of the MacArthur "Genius Award", Luís Alfaro's eye-opening rendition situates the iconic characters in the present-day world of the "Cholo" where the South Side Locos are Kings and Spanglish rules. Electricidad is mourning her father's body in her front yard, much to the dismay of the vecinos (neighbors) and her mother Clemencia, who was rumored to have had him killed to establish her power in the gang hierarchy. A comical bilingual chorus called "El Chisme" gossips and tries to save their barrio from inevitable cycles of violence.    eSe Teatro's presentation of Electricidad is a blend between a staged reading and a fully produced play, as is presented in Spanglish.

An evening of staged readings of short plays by local playwrights, directed and edited by Dinah Manoff and Renee Longstreet. Each of the entertaining plays is approximately ten minutes in length. Most are comedies and none of them have ever been performed.
sTheaterAddress: 200 Madison Avenue North, Bainbridge Island, WA 98110
sTicketPrice: Suggested donation $10; all proceeds benefit Helpline House

sSynopsis: Instead of performing Charles Dickens' beloved holiday classic for the umpteenth time, three actors decide to perform every Christmas story ever told ranging from classic movies like It's a Wonderful Life to quintessential Norelco-sponsored TV specials from the sixties --plus Christmas traditions from around the world, seasonal icons from ancient times to topical pop culture! A mad cap romp through the Holiday season!     Recommended for ages 8 and older.
showName: Every Christmas Story Ever Told (And Then Some)

sSynopsis: Coming back to ArtsWest is the reincarnation of sell-out phenomenon Evil Dead: The Musical,  the hilarious musical-comedy by George Reinblatt, Frank Cipolla,  Melissa Morris, and Christopher Bond. Five college students go to an  abandoned cabin in the woods and accidentally unleash an evil force that  turns them all into demons. It's all up to Ash and his trusty chainsaw  to save the day. Blood flies. Limbs are dismembered. Demons tell  jokes... and all is set to music.     Evil Dead: The Musical  is not included in the 6-show season package this year, however single  tickets are available to season ticket buyers upon purchase of a season  package-- months before tickets go on sale to the public.     Adult language, themes, graphic comedic scenes with lots and lots and lots of blood.  Recommended for ages 16 and older.

Gunderson's Emilie: La Marquise du Chatelet Defends Her Life Tonight wowed audiences after a very successful run last season. Now comes Exit, Pursued by a Bear, is a witty, moving, and razor sharp revenge comedy set in North Georgia Mountains. This feminist power-ballad tells a story about Nan Carter, a  smart, sassy, and resourceful woman on a war-path to get even with her spiteful husband. Nan can quote Shakespeare and Jimmy Carter, save a house cat and her life, and maybe even change the world.     Recommended for age 16 and older.

Fiddler on the Roof, Jr. transports audiences to Tsarist Russia in the early 1900s, to the small village of Anatevka. In Anatevka, Tevye, a poor dairyman, endeavors to keep the traditions of his close-knit Jewish community alive. Along with his wife Golde, Tevye attempts to raise five daughters, while also adjusting to a changing world. Rich in historical and ethnic detail, Fiddler on the Roof has impacted audiences around the world with its humor, warmth and honesty. Fiddler on the Roof is the winner of nine Tony Awards, including Best Musical, Best Composer/Lyricist, and Best Book of a Musical.

Johnny is certain he has found his soul mate in Frankie. Frankie is far more cautious and disinclined to jump to conclusions. A witty love story about what it takes to overcome our fears and take a chance on love. Winner of the Dramatists Guild Hull Warriner Award, written by Tony Award-winning playwright Terrence McNally.
showName: Frankie and Johnny in the Clair de Lune

sSynopsis: John Cummings is a lonely and divorced back-porch philosopher. Over three and a half years, three very different women occupy the apartment next door. As John reflects on his relationships with neighbors Fay, Angel & Gwen, he shares his unique views on everything from poets to sex.

An ambivalent Cinderella? A bloodthirsty Little Red Ridinghood? A Prince Charming with a roving eye? A Witch...who raps? They're all among the cockeyed characters in James Lapine and Stephen Sondheim's fractured fairy tale. When a Baker and his Wife learn they've been cursed with childlessness by the Witch next door, they embark on a quest for the special objects required to break the spell, swindling, lying to and stealing from Cinderella, Little Red, Rapunzel and Jack (the one who climbed the beanstalk). Everyone's wish is granted at the end of Act One, but the consequences of their actions return to haunt them later. What begins as a lively irreverent fantasy in the style of "The Princess Bride" becomes a moving lesson about community responsibility and the stories we tell our children.
sTheaterAddress: 7400 Sand Point Way NE, Seattle, WA 98115
theater: Seattle Musical Theatre,  Building #47, Magnuson Park

sSynopsis: Wedding bells aren't ringing, they're clanging at the union of this Jewish bride and Catholic groom! The Steinberg and Howard families couldn't have less in common…aside from the fact that their children are about to tie the knot. When the big day comes, frenzied wedding mayhem ensues--emotions run high, schemes unfold, and a twist in the plot hysterically unveils what no one saw coming. Bursting with clever lyrics and melodies that'll stick, It Shoulda Been You follows two families at odds as they reluctantly make their way down the aisle ultimately finding hope where they least expected it.
theater: Village Theatre - Francis J. Gaudette Theatre

sSynopsis: What do the Fates have in store for you? Why are you here?    All is revealed as Seattle cabaret luminaries Jayne Muirhead and John Engerman join forces to take you on a Fool's Journey of self discovery. Drawing on oracle traditions from Tarot to palmistry to astrology, each audience is treated to a unique evening of sublimely silly, unforgettable cabaret. Ancient themes collide with modern life as they twist classic tunes and blend forgotten gems with original songs.

Young Joey Stoshack has the special power to travel through time just by holding a baseball card and concentrating really hard. When he's given an assignment to write a paper on Jackie Robinson, it only makes sense to head back to 1947 and meet the famous baseball player.     Through his adventures, Joey experiences what it's like to be African-American during a time of segregation. He witnesses Jackie's dedication and determination when even people on his own team are against him.
sTheaterAddress: Second Avenue North and Thomas Street, Seattle, WA 98109
theater: Seattle Children's Theatre at Seattle Center

sSynopsis: Tracing the lives and life-long friendships of three southern women beginning in the Depression era and continuing through the early years of the new century, Lark Eden offers a lyrical exploration of the ties that bind lives together as tightly as family, and as surely as love.  From frog catching girls with skinned knees to world wizened grandmothers, Lark Eden follows these three lives through personal trials and victories no less daunting than the historical tribulations which provide the backdrop to these everyday American lives.

Collektor presents Sam Shepard's haunting and timeless drama of two divided families in the American West. Underscored by live music and performed by a cast of acclaimed Seattle actors, A Lie of the Mind is a darkly humorous, increasingly frenetic examination of generations torn apart by a marriage and brought together by an unspeakable act of violence.

A French shepherd sets out with his dog to plant a forest and transform a barren wasteland one acorn at a time in this charming tale from Puppet State Theatre Company of Scotland.     Hear the wind, feel the rain and smell the lavender in this multi-sensory theatrical delight. Based on Jean Giono's short story, this play is a unique blend of comedy and puppetry. It is an inspiring, ecologically-oriented tale of a human being who saw a need and decided not to ignore it but "to put things right." This uplifting and unforgettable story shows us the difference one man (and his dog!) can make in the world.
sTheaterAddress: Second Avenue North and Thomas Street, Seattle, WA 98109
theater: Seattle Children's Theatre at Seattle Center

sSynopsis: Manos - The Hands of Felt tells the story of Harold P. Warren, a man with a dream. A dream of filming a low budget horror film. But time is running out for Hal. Will uncooperative puppet actors, a ill-fated wrong turn and an evil cult spell his doom?    Inspired by Manos - The Hands of Fate, Mystery Science Theater 3000, and the story behind "Manos", Manos - The Hands of Felt features characters, scenes and songs from the original movie, cut with a healthy dose of puppet mayhem.

Based on a true story, My Mother's Lesbian Jewish Wiccan Wedding is a hilarious and touching musical about a mother, in the midst of an identity-crisis, and her teenage son. A new job brings new opportunities and a chance to truly find herself, discover her own sexuality, rediscover her faith, and eventually come out to her son, ex-husband, and even her  homophobic Jewish mother. Musical numbers include: "If You Love Me," "Don't Take Your Lesbian Moms to Hooters," and "A Short History of Gay Marriage in Canada." A true story- musical-comedy for anyone who's ever been in love.     Recommended for ages 13 and older.
showName: My Mother's Lesbian Jewish Wiccan Wedding

sSynopsis: My Time with the Lady is an original play by Ron Richardson and John Longenbaugh that tells of the life and times of The Lusty Lady Peepshow, through the eyes of a young man who worked the front desk.

Watch the hilarious Little Sisters of Hoboken display their divine talents in a zany benefit revue. In an effort to raise money for their fallen Sisters--unfortunate victims of a convent cooking accident--Mother Superior and her order of eccentric and endearing nuns show the lighter side of being Catholic.     With riotous dance numbers, show-stopping songs and side-splitting wit, you'll swear the music and comedy of Nunsense was heaven-sent!

In a small corner of Ireland circa 1918, a stuffed goat living atop a garbage heap concocts a magical inner world to escape the reality of its bleak existence. Award-winning playwright Glen Berger weaves a fantastical narrative of love-struck soldiers, mermaids, unicorns, and a hapless inventor attempting to devise a self-flushing toilet. Suffused with music from World War I, O Lovely Glowworm is a joyously inventive celebration of humanity.

Arguably the funniest comedy ever, this Neil Simon classic is one of the most famed stage plays in American history. Meet Oscar Madison, a carefree, positively unkempt, divorcé, and his new roomie, Felix Unger, an uptight, fastidious man, recently separated from his wife and practically suicidal. While it would seem that bunking together would be a last resort for these two, the decision to do so mixes slob with neat-freak, leading to total madness for them, and laugh-out-loud comedy for us!
theater: Village Theatre - Francis J. Gaudette Theatre

sSynopsis: Mel Brooks' record-breaking, 12-time Tony Award-winner, The Producers is a hysterically outrageous hit! When an out-of-luck Broadway producer and his nervous accountant hatch a plan to mount a guaranteed Broadway flop in order to turn some quick cash, their wrongful scheming goes wildly awry. With swingin' tunes and a vaudeville feel, this show is loaded with laughs and dazzling choreography that is sure to leave stars in your eyes.
theater: Village Theatre - Francis J. Gaudette Theatre

sSynopsis: UMO Ensemble goes Zen - the Northwest's most acclaimed physical theatre company brings their irreverent approach to ancient tales of wonder. Red nose monk clowns tackle Buddhist, Zen and Sufi stories through mask, puppets, music, laughter - and breathtaking physical skill.     The UMO Ensemble monk clowns each tackle a different life problem... dangling from a rope, juggling or balancing...singing and clowning. Zen Tales is a delight for the whole family.

Norman and Ethel spend every summer at their lake house in Maine. When their daughter visits one year, she brings a boyfriend and his son along - hoping her parents will look after the boy while she and her fiancé go off traveling. A heartwarming play about relationships that sometimes take a lifetime to unfold.

Conservative Ben Gerard doesn't understand his 15-year-old daughter, Christi, who bitterly tries to exert her independence. Mimi, the wife and mother, tries to straddle the widening gulf between father and daughter during a family "vacation." A wistful stranger, Violet Aldrich, appears, but is it too late to salvage the family? "Hitchcockian" suspense that leads to a shocking ending.

Little Voice is a young woman with a hidden talent: she can emulate every chanteuse from Judy Garland to Edith Piaf. She hides in her room, crooning and dreaming of love, while her disheveled mother, Mari, mistakes a seedy talent agent's interest as affection rather than enthusiasm for the gold mine buried in her daughter's throat. An engaging fairy tale of despair, love, and hope as "L.V." finds a voice of her own.     Recommended for ages 16 and older.
showName: The Rise And Fall Of Little Voice

sSynopsis: Sex in Seattle is back! SIS Productions celebrates its 10th Anniversary with its penultimate episode! Tess, Chloe, Elizabeth and Jenna have finally found true love. Or have they? Thoughts of the one that got away can interfere with even the happiest of relationships. And how can reality ever compete with the person of one's dreams? Newcomers and long-time fans will want to catch Sex in Seattle before it goes away! Don't miss the country's longest-running quirky romantic comedy about contemporary Asian American women, their lives and their loves.
showName: Sex In Seattle Episode 19: The One That Got Away

sSynopsis: Sick is a breathtaking solo performance about a woman's fight to hang on to a fraying thread of connection to her self. After she is thrown down the rabbit hole of misdiagnosis and medication she journeys with her doctors and her mom to the most unlikely, absurd, and terrifying places.    Elizabeth Kenny, one of Seattle's most masterful monologists, was a healthy thirty-two year-old woman who went to the doctor for a common ailment. A year and a half later, she was being escorted, by hospital orderlies, to a coffee shop along with the rest of the level 5 patients from the psych ward. Her gripping -- and often hilarious -- story unfolds in a unique performance that uses chance operation to skillfully reveal how she got from here to there.

Princess Beauty is a cutie, but being pretty doesn't cut it when you really want to slay dragons and find adventure. Will Beauty get to be her very own hero - or will she be interrupted by a 100-year nap? Will the Prince save her - or will she save him? (This version isn't just for little girls - the boys will love it too!)    April 23rd - May 1st at Kirkland Performance Center  May 7th & 8th at Renton Carco Theater   May  15th at Seattle Museum of History & Industry

"It's not a story. It's my life!" What happens when your life is at stake, and the only chance you have at survival lies in the hands of a complete stranger? Take Me America follows the brutal process of several struggling refugees in their quest for asylum in the United States and the INS agents who are responsible for deciding their fates. As the dreams and fears of each refugee come to light, the INS agents struggle to find balance between their feelings for humanity, and the reality of their professional position. Inspired by true stories, this new musical balances heavy themes with light-hearted comedy that compliments a gripping, rock score.
theater: Village Theatre - Francis J. Gaudette Theatre

sSynopsis: Winner of two Tony® Awards for Best Play and a Pulitzer Prize, Angels in America melds love, hate, religion, and politics into a uniquely American epic.  The year is 1985.  In New York City, Roy Cohn, the politically powerful right-wing lawyer angrily denies his diagnosis of AIDS while his protégé - a court clerk and Republican Mormon - struggles with a Valium-addicted wife.  Simultaneously, an abandoned yet spirited gay man begins to hear messages from a supernatural being that build to an exhilarating conclusion.    Single tickets go on sale July 1st.
showName: Angels in America, Part One:  Millennium Approaches

sSynopsis: Oscar Levant shares his stories, his music, fears, aspirations, struggles, and joys in this rollicking, musical, comic, and compassionate look at the great composer and pianist's life and work.

A Shepard classic, the story centers on two brothers, who at the beginning of the play are as different as night and day. Disillusioned, and meeting after a long absence, the brothers find that what they each really want is to be the other.    Presented by Sound Counsel Realty.
sTheaterAddress: 200 Madison Avenue North, Bainbridge Island, WA 98110

sSynopsis: Featuring three episodes straight from the classic TV series:  Time Enough at Last  The Obsolete Man  The Monsters are Due on Maple Street    Directed by long time Schmee Alum, Tim Moore (who also will play "Rod"),  The Twilight Zone: Live! brings back to life all the Cold War era's anxieties and angst, paranoia and paradoxes. A long time audience favorite at The Schmee, The Twilight Zone: Live! breathes new life into these trusted tales of a simpler time, when the aliens wore silly hats, and the enemy always came from without.

AUTO is a movement installation that takes place in and around a moving vehicle. Using the landscape of a parking garage, audience members move and are moved through a series of performance vignettes that inhabit the at once private and public space that is a car.     AUTO investigates the body of performer/driver, the body of witness/passenger, and the body of the car itself. It explores how we communicate when we are encased in a small piece of metal that can speed, stop, lock us in, blow us up, or crash at any moment.

Theater Schmeater welcomes audiences to another installment of The Twilight Zone: Live!, where they will be whisked to a dimension where cold war fear and paranoia are a deadly reality. Each night the audience will be led through three classic episodes from the iconic TX series.

Philadelphia Premiere    Welcome to Shirley State College, Vermont where it's Body Awareness Week.  In charge of the week's festivities, college professor Phyllis has anything but a conventional life with girlfriend Joyce and her son Jared.  But when a visiting artist brings his photographs of nude women into their home, conflicting feelings over sexuality and identity get passionately stirred up.  Nominated for the Drama Desk Best New Play award, Body Awareness is a hilarious send-up of political correctness is fresh from Obie award winning playwright Annie Baker (Circle Mirror Transformation, The Aliens).    Single tickets go on sale July 1st.

1812 Productions presents Neil Simon's Laughter On The 23rd Floor, directed by Matt Pfeiffer.    McCarthy's blacklist, the FBI, a big bully Television Network, and a who's who of comedy legends-to-be. It's the 1950s in America and the fight to be funny is on. Simon's classic comedy takes us to the legendary writer's room for Sid Caesar's variety comedy program Your Show of Shows.     Laughter on the 23rd Floor is a fabled account of how writers Mel Brooks, Woody Allen, Carl Reiner, Larry Gelbart, and others matched wit to wit and punchline to punchline to make comedy history.

B. Someday Productions presents the world premiere of Mistaken Charity, written & directed by Stan Heleva, based on original stories by Sarah Orne Jewett and Mary Wilkins Freeman.    The play is set in a dilapidated, moss-covered sharecropper's shack in the middle of rural Maine in 1906, and shows us the endearing adventures of two elderly, impoverished and handicapped women who are forced from their home by "well-meaning" neighbors and get ticked off!

1812 Productions presents Our Show of Shows!, as part of its Phoebe and Otto Premiere Series. The work is written and performed by  David Ingram, Tony Lawton, Jennifer Childs, and Dave Jadico, and directed by Jennifer Childs.    Playing in tandem with Laughter on the 23rd Floor, the production takes the exuberant comedy of Sid Caesar's writer's room and brings it center stage. À la Your Show of Shows, 1812's Our Show of Shows features vintage and original material performed in 1812's signature style.

Perô or the Mysteries of the Night is performed in English and features actor/singers, puppets, live music, and is recommended for ages 6 and older.    Perô is a baker in a tiny Italian village where he works all night to bake his bread. He is too shy to tell the girl he has loved since childhood of his feelings. She is Colombina, the village laundress, and she does her work in the sunlight. When Colombina runs off with a flashy house painter, Perô's heart is broken and he closes his shop -- too sad to bake for the village. This charming musical play tells a story of love while contrasting night and day and bashful and bold.
showName: Pero, or the Mysteries of the Night
sTicketPrice: General Admission Adults $15.00 and children (up to 12 years) $12.00

sSynopsis: Art is made up of moments. Moments of inspiration. Power. Emotion. Grace. Passion. These moments collided in Paris in 1911 and changed the path of art and conventional creativity. There will be another spectacular convergence exactly 100 years later.    Philadelphia, April 7, 2011 - May 1, 2011. Introducing the Philadelphia International Festival of the Arts.    The festival will feature artistic expression from across the region and around the world. And the world will be invited to join Philadelphia in a new moment of innovation, collaboration and creativity.
showName: Philadelphia International Festival of the Arts

sSynopsis: "Freedom is just a fleeting moment of relief between oppressors"- Prometheus.  Renegade Classic Theatre seeks to produce works that are foreign.  Foreign in their origin or their content.  We celebrate and give voice to the lesser known and voiceless. A Prometheus Bound: A Folk Musical riffs on Aeschylus' classic work by setting it in 1930's Oklahoma during the Dust Bowl Era.  Prometheus follows suit like other folk heroes of the time such as Tom Joad, Woody Guthrie, and Pete Seeger.  The production is greatly influenced by Guthrie's life and music, Steinbeck's portrayal of America, and the Dust Bowl photographs of Dorothea Lange.
showName: A Prometheus Bound: A Folk Musical

sSynopsis: Two of Shakespeare's insignificant characters get a play of their own in Tom Stoppard's comedic masterpiece Rosencrantz and Guildenstern are Dead. The play tells the story of Hamlet from the point of view of his school-friends-turned-spies as they struggle against their fate and the play's inevitable conclusion. Stoppard's nimble wit, command of language, and enthusiasm for the absurd shine in this: his most recognizable play.

From the author of Black Gold comes a poignant comedy The New York Times called "irreverent," "amusing," and "sweet-natured." Inspired by real-life events, Two Jews Walk Into a War... follows Ishaq and Zeblyan, the last two Jews in Afghanistan. They share the only remaining synagogue that has not been destroyed by the Taliban. They share a desire to continue practicing their religion and to repopulate the Jewish community in Kabul. They share a mutual hatred of each other. Can one incredible act of faith keep the diaspora alive and keep this Middle Eastern odd couple from killing each other?
showName: Two Jews Walk into a War...

sSynopsis: Under the Same Moon is a hilarious comedy about budding entrepreneurs and best friends, Rita Jones and Thelma Lou Greene, who partner to open a beauty parlor. They find the perfect location but there's only one hitch, it's right smack dab next door to Burt Carlson's barbershop. A man who thinks the only place for a woman is at home cooking, cleaning and taking care of children. Burt will go to any end to rid himself of his new neighbors.

Broadway's Smash Hit Comedy Thriller The 39 Steps mixes a Hitchcock masterpiece with a juicy spy novel. Add a dash of Monty Python and you have this hilarious Tony Award-winning hit! A beautiful spy leaks a deadly secret to a man she's just met. With that, our hero suddenly finds himself embroiled in a high-speed chase across England and Scotland, dodging police, charming ladies, and uncovering clues at every turn. The mind-blowing cast of four plays 150 characters!

Winner of Broadway's Tony and Drama Critics Circle Awards for "Best Play" as well as London's Olivier and Evening Standard Awards for "Best Comedy," Art is a wickedly witty portrait of modern art and old-fashioned friendships creating a conflict between friendships and values as three prosperous middle-aged, longtime American friends, living in Paris, come to blows over the value of a very expensive piece of art. According to Newsweek "...at times Art sounds like a marriage of Moliere and Woody Allen...hilarious (and) sneakily profound..."    Serge (played by Alexander Kulcsar of Fairfield) has purchased a work of art which has cost him nearly - two hundred thousand francs. His friend Marc (played by Pat Leo of Monroe) is loath to believe that any friend of his would spend so much money on what to him is merely a white canvas. Another friend, Yvan (played by Dan Arenovski of Milford), tries to calm the dispute between the other two, but while trying to appease both, ignites the quarrel which forces all three men to re-examine their friendship and the direction in which it is moving.

Playhouse Theatre Group, Inc. brings Stages on the Sound's acclaimed adaptation of William Shakespeare's The Comedy of Errors to Playhouse on Park.  In this hysterical and contemporary adaptation, the classic tale is performed with four actors playing all of the roles!  The play centers around the separation, and ongoing search between a husband, wife and two sets of identical twins.  Suspense and hilarity ensue before the family is reunited.  This is Shakespeare in its most accessible form.     David Fuller, of NewYorkTheatre.com, says: "You should go. You will laugh, you will smile constantly, and you will consistently wonder at how in the heck they are able to pull off Shakespeare's complete comedy with just four actors!"
sTheaterAddress: 244 Park Road, Hartford / West Hartford, Connecticut 06119

sSynopsis: Cutman is the dramatic story of a young Jewish boxer who dreams of being the Welter-Weight Champion of the World.  Trained by his father in the basement of their synagogue, he turns pro and takes the boxing world by storm.  But when his shot at the title fight is scheduled on the eve of Yom Kippur, he must choose between achieving his lifelong dream and defying his faith.  From rock to pop to hip-hop to R&B, Cutman boasts a contemporary score that is sure to pack a knockout punch. This new musical stars Robert Cuccioli and Cory Grant.

Luna's Sea is the story of a young child named Luna who is swept up into a mysterious puppet theater on the beach. Guided by a gentle moon-puppeteer, she journeys deeper and deeper into the ocean and experiences her own fascination and interpretation of the sea. Through the use of dance, puppetry, optical illusions and black light theater, Luna and the audience travel from the penguin inhabited shores of Africa through tides of elegant flying sting rays to the dark underwater homelands of bioluminescent animals, and in the end discover that all life on earth is ultimately connected.     The magical voyage of Luna's Sea offers families with children under 12 a unique attraction that both educates and entertains. At the conclusion of the production, the journey continues when guests participate in a treasure hunt through Olde Mistick Village and are then admitted to Mystic Aquarium. During the treasure hunt, participants will have to find the secret Luna logos hidden within the village to receive a special reward. The fun continues with a visit to Mystic Aquarium where families and friends experience many of the animals that were depicted in Luna's Sea.
sTheaterAddress: Olde Mistick Village 27 Coogan Boulevard, Mystic, Connecticut 06355

sSynopsis: Playhouse on Park is proud to present stop/time dance theater in a new production, titled Swing Set. The company will surprise you with their take on the swing era which will have a mix of traditional swing, tap and even hip hop..  Stop/Time's annual dance performance is a favorite at Playhouse on Park.  Buy your tickets early!  Swing Set is conceived and directed by Darlene Zoller.      Darlene Zoller is the founder of stop/time dance theater, and co-founder and Artistic Director of Playhouse on Park.  She teaches at the Hartt School Community Division, Glastonbury Dance Center and Court House Plus.  She has also choreographed for the Manchester Musical Players, Mark Twain Masquers, CT Cabaret Theater, Little Theater of Manchester, Glastonbury High School and Hall High School's Pops 'n Jazz.     Opening night, Thursday, April 28th includes a complimentary wine and cheese from 6:30pm - 7:30pm.   Call for group and school rates.
sTheaterAddress: 244 Park Road, Hartford / West Hartford, Connecticut 06119

sSynopsis: Roundabout Theatre Company presents a new Broadway production of Anything Goes, starring Tony Award winner Sutton Foster as Reno Sweeney and Joel Grey as Moonface Martin. Tony Award winner Kathleen Marshall directs and choreographs.    Anything Goes features music & lyrics by Cole Porter; original book by P.G. Wodehouse & Guy Bolton and Howard Lindsay & Russel Crouse; and a new book by Timothy Crouse and John Weidman.      ALL ABOARD for this saucy and splendid new production of Cole Porter\'s musical romp across the Atlantic.  When the S.S. American heads out to sea, etiquette and convention head out the portholes as two unlikely pairs set off on the course to true love... proving that sometimes destiny needs a little help from a crew of singing sailors, an exotic disguise and some good old-fashioned blackmail.    Peppering this hilariously bumpy ride are some of musical theater's most memorable standards, including "You're the Top," "Blow, Gabriel, Blow," "It's De-Lovely," "I Get A Kick Out of You," and "Anything Goes."

This is definitely not the same old song and dance. It's every parent's nightmare. Your little girl has suddenly become a young woman, and what's worse, has fallen deliriously in love with a sweet, smart young man from a respectable family.

Old friends reunite over bourbon on ice to reflect upon the shadows of their lives.  Fifty years of love, friendship, and rivalry are put to the test at the barrel of a shotgun in this gritty new play by Pulitzer Prize-winner Sam Shepard.  The characters are older and the booze goes down a little harder as Shepard spins a poignant hangdog tale of remorse and regret for two men at the twilight of life's journey into night.
theater: Contemporary American Theater Festival - Frank Center Stage

sSynopsis: Barriolesque Performance Carnivale done Urban Style is a theatrical variety show featuring some of the hottest & unique performers and themes. Barriolesque provides an outlet for these artists to showcase their talent.    Featured every month is the Barriolesque Birthday Celebration. Come celebrate your BIRTHDAY with us!!!! The Barriolesque Way!!    Evolved from its open mic roots of words, rhythms, sounds, dance, and rituals originating out of Spanish Harlem's Carlito's Café to a performance carnivale done urban style at the Lower East Side's Nuyorican Poet's Café.     Now Barriolesque is coming home to the Poet's Den in Spanish Harlem and will feature a vast array of talent: including spoken word artists, comedians, rappers, dancers, musicians, and singers.
showName: Barriolesque Performance Carnivale done Urban Style

sSynopsis: A hilarious and touching evening of theater celebrating a beloved daughter of Texas.
showName: Ann: An Affectionate Portrate of Ann Richards

sSynopsis: When aliens abduct a large drag queen and drop her in a teeny Garden of Eden, will she have room to fall from grace? International cabaret sensation Joey Arias and Obie Award-winning puppeteer Basil Twist team up for an eye-popping musical tour, from Genesis to risque universes beyond imagination.
In its fifth season, Broadway legend Barbara Cook continues to shine the spotlight on her top-notch   Broadway peers.
A celebration of one young boy's triumph against the odds.

African Continuum Theatre Company presents Blues for an Alabama Sky, by Pearl Cleage.    It is the summer of 1930 in Harlem, New York. The creative euphoria of the Harlem Renaissance has given way to the harsher realities of the Great Depression. The play brings together a rich cast of characters who reflect the conflicting currents of the time through their overlapping personalities and politics. Invoking the image of African American expatriate extraordinaire, Josephine Baker, as both muse and myth, Cleage's characters struggle to look beyond 125th Street for the fulfillment of their dreams.
by Charles L. Mee  directed by Derek Goldman    A whimsical, fantastical, and joyous celebration of the art in everyday life.

Prepare yourself: in the parking lot of a mega craft store in Idaho, someone is summoning the Rapture. Samuel D. Hunter's heart breakingly funny reckoning between a father and son will shatter your preconceptions about the sacred, the profane, and the secret lives of big box retailers.

Epic problems. Limited space. The average American spends more than 80 minutes a day in their car. Taffety Punk offers three unique one-act plays that share one vital element: the car. It's a human demolition derby as the characters race, swerve, and collide with each other all within the narrow confines of their passenger seats. Get in! It will only take about 80 minutes.
Three Caucasian men sing, dance, and irreverently march their way through 4,000 years of Chinese history in China: The Whole Enchilada, presented by Landless Theatre Company.

Does humanity have an expiration date? Four hungry friends from grad school face the dawn of the recession in this scathing satire of American enterprise and ingenuity. But while they're busy cooking up schemes for love and success, the beasts of agribusiness are closing in...

When Frieda brings Heinrich her husband's beloved cuckoo clock to be repaired, they embark on a race against time to solve a mysterious puzzle. Part comic love story, part murder mystery, The Clockmaker, by Stephen Massicotte is an entrancing look at how relationships can change how we see the world, that the time we spend with people can be hell or heaven on earth.

The Color Purple, based on Alice Walker's novel of the same name, is an inspiring family saga that tells the unforgettable story of a woman, who, through love, finds the strength to triumph over adversity and discover her unique voice in the world.     With a moving book and a score featuring gospel, jazz, ragtime and the blues, the musical is ultimately a story of hope, a testament to the healing power of love, and a celebration of life.
Featuring Sinatra's vocals and a live on-stage big band, the production is set in a nightclub where four couples search for love.

Altar Boyz is a foot-stomping, rafter-raising, sidesplitting, award-winning musical comedy about a fictitious Catholic boy-band on the last night of their "Raise the Praise" tour. These boys are five all-singing, all dancing heartthrobs from Ohio: Matthew, Mark, Luke, Juan and Abraham. With right harmony, irreverent humor and sinfully spectacular choreography, they joyously deliver a message of unity - ?there is not a star as bright as its constellation, no harmony in a single voice.
Rasputin: healer or hedonist or both? Playwright Jason Craig, composer Dave Malloy, and director Patrick Dooley delve into the world of Russia's infamous bad boy mystic.

Betty Buckley celebrates her return to the Bay Area & her debut at The RRazz Room at Hotel Nikko. This show is for all lovers of Broadway and great music. A must see! In an exclusive one-week only run of the new show For The Love Of Broadway, Ms. Buckley will perform theater songs she's always wanted to sing from shows like "South Pacific," "The Pajama Game," "The King and I," "Avenue Q" and "Nine." Emmy and Grammy Award winner John McDaniel serves as musical consultant & has provided special material.

Up and coming vocalist Bill Kwan returns to the Rrazz Room after his sold out CD release concert in support of his debut album "Pentimento". With warmth and earnest storytelling he melds pop and jazz genres to great effect featuring diverse music from the likes of Irving Berlin to Neil Young.  Often compared to James Taylor and Chet Baker, with a dash of Diana Krall; Bill takes a hip and refreshing approach to classic and contemporary material and reinterprets them for today's audience.  Please join Bill and his band on a thoroughly enjoyable evening of beautiful and sensual music that spans decades of popular song.    "Pentimento" now available on iTunes and Amazon

The Tony award-winning musical, Cabaret, tells the tale of a young American writer whose life is turned upside down when he settles in 1929 Berlin. It's a time when the world economy was in turmoil and World War II was on the horizon...and when the only escape from reality was at the provocative Kit Kat Klub cabaret.

Ever since Carly discovered the voice of Freddie Mercury, she has been in love with his theatrical, rocker glam persona. Freddie Mercury could sing anything, in any style, and that alone is an art to celebrate. Carly will be Queen for a day, paying homage to her idol, and sharing historic and interesting facts about Mercury's public and intimate lifestyle. Carly relates to Mercury's flair for theatrical and dramatic performing, incorporating his work into a night of fabulous cabaret.
showName: Carly Ozard: Somebody to Love; My Musicial Tribute To Freddie Mercury

sSynopsis: This tantalizing tale of treachery, murder, fame and fortune is electrified with exhilarating dance numbers and show-stopping tunes. Known both for its choreography by the famed Bob Fosse and the 2002 movie, which won six Academy Awards, the show flaunts celebrity, scandal, and corruption in Jazz-age Chicago.
sTheaterAddress: W. San Carlos Street, San Jose, CA 95113

sSynopsis: "Dilley shines... his falsetto wowing." - Backstage    "A handsome and engaging presence... Dilley is a powerful tenor with a strong falsetto range... Dilley proved he has a keen ear for picking gems." - Bay Area Reporter    Chris Dilley returns to the Rrazz Room by popular demand! Featuring his soaring tenor, eclectic music choices and energetic stage presence, Chris brings another fabulous night of music and fun to his beloved San Francisco.

A collection of six one-act plays by American writers.    It's an evening of laughs when 6th Street Playhouse presents a collection of one act plays by great American writers.     Plays include "Your Mother's Butt," by Allan Ball; "Sure Thing" and "Variations on the Death of Trosky," both by David Ives; "The Actor's Nightmare," by Christopher Durang; "The Ties That Bind," by Eric Cible; and "The Tarantino Variation," by Seth Kramer. Directed by Robin Miller and featuring Laura J. Davies, Terry Gault, Nancy Lawson, Autumn Mirassou, Ray Morgan, James Pelican and Jesse Pennington.

Mark Twain's wisecracking hero finds himself zapped from 1880 to the Middle Ages, from industrial America to medieval England. Yankee can-do spirit enables this crafty time-traveler to drag a backward culture kicking and screaming into the modern era--but only for a while. Breathtaking, hilarious-- and shockingly relevant to 21st century America.
sTheaterAddress: 1220 Pear Avenue, Unit K, Mountain View, CA 94043
showName: A Connecticut Yankee in King Arthur's Court

sSynopsis: Time and space are transcended as we witness Cordelia, wrapped in memory, trapped in a shadowy world, bearing the weight of her own actions. This intimate echo of Shakespeare's King Lear from Cordelia's point of view is informed by the Japanese Noh "phantasmal warrior" play. Cordelia speaks to all of us who wonder how to be good to others while being true to ourselves.

Life isn't easy for the MaGrath sisters of Hazlehurst, Mississippi. Lenny's horse is dead, Meg's singing career is dead and Babe's husband is near-dead (because she shot him!). But nothing -- not meddling cousins, nor past and present lovers, nor a touch of mental illness -- can keep these women down. Beth Henley's Pulitzer Prize-winning comedy puts the "fun" back in dysfunctional. Henley may heap tragedy after tragedy upon her heroines but does so with love, compassion and a surprising sense of humor.

Del Shores' A Sordid Affair is headlined by "Sordid Lives" mastermind Del Shores who tells his Sordid tales from his sold-out stand-up tour and more. Del's special guests include everybody's favorite "Aunt LaVonda" Ann Walker, Rosemary Alexander ("Dr. Eve") and Newell Alexander ("Wardell"), along with Jason Dottley ("Ty"). "A collection of stand-up and music that was so funny it had the audience doing spit-takes between standing ovations." ~Joy Tipping, Dallas Morning News
showName: Del Shores: A Sordid Affair with the Nation of Jason Tour 2011

sSynopsis: Molière's classic comedy comes to uproarious new life in a clever and contemporary adaptation from one of Berkeley Rep's favorite artists. Steven Epp delighted audiences as Figaro and The Miser--now he's back with A Doctor in Spite of Himself. The traditional story of a girl feigning illness to avoid an unwanted wedding erupts into hilarity when Epp decides to play doctor. In a pitch-perfect production punctuated with live music, this ridiculous physician proves that love and laughter remain life's best medicine.
showName: A Doctor in Spite of Himself

sSynopsis: Known as "the nightingale of the Delta," Alma Winemiller is a lonely, sensitive misfit hemmed in by her stern, puritanical father and her unstable mother. Rebellious, with an artistic temperament that her father tries to suppress, Alma finds consolation in her music and in the secret lifelong love she has for the boy-next-door.     In honor of playwright Tennessee Williams' 100th birthday, Artistic Director Tom Ross helms this powerful play filled with all of the majestic themes, oversized characters, and gentle poetry that has earned Williams his exalted position in American theatre.

The Tabard Theatre Company presents Inferno Theatre Company's production of Galileo's Daughters, which was written, directed and designed by Guilio Cesare Perrone.    Through the lens of a father's loving relationship with his two religious daughters, this show examines the relationship between science and religion and how they serve the pursuit of knowledge and truth.
sTheaterAddress: 29 North San Pedro  Street, San Jose, CA 95110

sSynopsis: Direct from Indonesia    Didik Nini Thowok's fame propelled him throughout Indonesia for his unique style; combining classical, folk, modern and comedic dance form. He is one of the few artists who continues the long tradition of "Traditional Cross-Gender" in dance form. He is skilled in various dance traditions such as topeng (mask dance), Sundanese, Cirebon, Balinese, and of course Central Javanese; He has performed for the highest dignitaries throughout the world and this will be his fourth visit to the United States. Didik Nini Thowok Dance Studio teaches many styles of dance, including Central Javanese, Sundanese, Cirebon Mask Dance, Balinese, and Original Choreography.
sTheaterAddress: 25 Van Ness Avenue, San Francisco, CA 94102

sSynopsis: World-premiere production  When Jon was a boy, his father was shot--and suddenly their lives were part of history. Years later, when staging a production of Hamlet, the son must confront his buried feelings about a crime that shocked the nation. In this evocative new play, Artistic Director Tony Taccone imagines a fable for San Francisco based on the assassination of Mayor George Moscone. The ghost of the king stalks the battlements of a boy's mind--and speaks to all of us about love and loss. A poetic collage of fiction and memory, this world-premiere production is staged by none other than Jonathan Moscone.

World Premiere    Every family creates a sacred story out of love. In Bill Cain's poignant new play, a man moves in with his mother when she becomes too frail to care for herself. Their reunion heals old wounds, opening a heartfelt and humorous new chapter in their relationship. From the award-winning author of Equivocation and 9 Circles, this timeless tale celebrates a mother's love and a son's devotion. Respected director Kent Nicholson comes back to the Bay Area for the world premiere of How to Write a New Book for the Bible.
showName: How to Write a New Book for the Bible

sSynopsis: Hugh Jackman performs his Broadway and Hollywood favorite musical numbers backed by a 17 piece orchestra.

Join A.C.T. for a new staging of one of Euripides' most beautifully written plays, Ion. Filled with false prophecies and mysterious family secrets, Ion  traces the dramatic chain of events that unfolds when the god Apollo disrupts the lives of a royal family, stirring up catastrophe, confusion, and--at long last--happy resolution.     This fresh take on a classic work features the A.C.T. M.F.A. Program class of 2012.

Directed by Sarna Lapine, this theatrical cabaret brings the audience on a roaring '20s ride through love, heartbreak, and everything in between. An old-fashioned evening of entertainment told from the perspective of a modern girl and the eccentric characters she inhabits. Broadway, film and TV star Emily Bergl, with acclaimed musical director and pianist G. Scott Lacy, create a cabaret world that blends classic hits with vintage takes on modern favorites from Roy Orbison to Madonna.

The Kinsey Sicks combine rich, four-part harmony, biting satire and over-the-top drag. In Each Hit & I, the girls treat us to an evening of politics, personal revelations, social critique, sexual foibles and plain old raunch - all in glorious four-part harmony. THE KINSEY SICKS, America's Favorite Dragapella Beautyshop Quartet, assault all the senses in their brand new musical show. THE KINSEY SICKS promise you that you will not be disappointed. You'll be appalled, but not disappointed.
showName: The Kinsey Sicks: Each Hit & I

sSynopsis: EMMY AWARD WINNING STAR OF TV'S "WILL & GRACE"    BRAND NEW HOLIDAY SHOW - SAN FRANCISCO PREMIER!    Somewhat of a departure from Jordan's usual autobiographical style, Deck Them Halls, Ya'll is an evening of characters lamenting or celebrating the Christmas season. Jordan goes full out on this one with costumes and music. In his words, "Honey, it's a dog and pony show!" Deck Them Halls, Ya'll! is both scream out loud funny and life affirming while rolling to a very, very surprising conclusion.
showName: Leslie Jordan: Deck Them Halls, Ya'll!

sSynopsis: Shakespeare's Associates presents Pulitzer Prize winner David Mamet's "hilarious and heartfelt look at two actors battling to share a dressing room and the spotlight ... an inside and often outrageous look at the world of show business."     Shakespeare's Associates is the Tri-Valley's professional theater, voted 2010 "Best Place to Get the Shakes" by the East Bay Express. The Bothwell Arts Center's West End Theater is located just a few minutes from historic downtown Livermore--enjoy a bite in a bistro and a glass of vintage before catching Mamet's laugh-out-loud homage to the theater!
A hilarious and heartfelt look at two actors battling to share a dressing room and the spotlight...an inside and often outrageous look at the world of show business.
theater: West End Theater at the Bothwell Art Center

sSynopsis: When a flower falls in love with a blushing bride, can he complete a quest to become a man and win her love? Should he? Playwright and burlesque performer Taylor Mac, along with dozens of local Bay Area artists, tackle love, marriage, and Prop 8-using vaudeville, haiku, drag queens, ukuleles, feminist theories, dream ballets, public dressing rooms, and everything else in Mr. Mac's theatrical arsenal, A fantastical cornucopia of theatre, party, circus, and social experiment, The Lily's Revenge cross examines with humor, heart, and irreverence one of our oldest institutions.    The Lily's Revenge is a rolling world premiere with Magic Theatre, HERE Arts Center (New York), Southern Rep Theatre (New Orleans), and The National Theatre of Scotland.
sTheaterAddress: Building D, Fort Mason Center, San Francisco, CA 94123

sSynopsis: Live Stand-up Comedy Showcase and music with Groovy Judy at 4 STAR Movie Theatre.    Hosted by Danny Dechi - Comedian and world's only pencil musician.    Featuring Top Bay Area Comedians: Steven Pearl headlines, with Kenny Altman, Kevin Monroe, Kurt Weitzmann, Rebecca Arthur, Tessie Chua, Veronica Porras.

Believe it or not, Lucie Arnaz is celebrating 40 plus years in show business. She began her long career in a recurring role on television on The Lucy Show, opposite her mother, Lucille Ball. At age 15, she became a series regular on Here's Lucy, a show which ran for six seasons. She starred in her own series, The Lucie Arnaz Show and later in the critically acclaimed Sons & Daughters on CBS. On piano, Musical Director Ron Abel joins Lucie for a night of songs, memories, and love Lulu style.
showName: Lucie Arnaz: Lulu's Back In Town!

sSynopsis: The Award-winning Custom Made Theatre Co. presents a dynamic new staging of David Henry Hwang's modern classic.    A French diplomat carried on a twenty-year affair with a Chinese actor and opera singer, not realizing that his partner was a man masquerading as a woman. From these basic facts comes a sensational drama that wonders how such a fantasy can take hold, and what illusions exist between men and women, as well as between East and West.     Interwoven with the Puccini opera, M. Butterfly is a timeless, and highly theatrical, story of love and betrayal.

Few companies can electrify an audience like the Alvin Ailey American Dance Theater, whose captivating energy makes every performance a life-affirming experience. The Ailey dancers have dazzled audiences worldwide for over 50 years, their unparalleled artistry fulfilling Ailey's vision that dance is for everybody. Don't miss this magnificent company in a program featuring Ailey's signature masterpiece, Revelations, which uses African-American spirituals and holy blues to explore the places of deepest grief and utmost joy in the soul.

Manchester's music has established her as a compelling singer/songwriter. She co-wrote "Whenever I Call You Friend" with Kenny Loggins, which became a radio classic. In addition, her songs have been recorded by Barbra Streisand, Dusty Springfield, Alison Krauss, and many others. Manchester wrote the score for Disney's "Mouse Detective" and "Lady & The Tramp II," released her 16th CD and celebrated four decades of performing all at the same time.

The Giver, based on the Newberry Award winning novel, questions the wisdom of a society that has eliminated pain and suffering as well as emotion, colors, animals and nature. The Giver tells the story of Jonas, a 12-year-old boy, who is chosen as the Receiver of Memory by his society.
theater: Court House Center for the Arts

sSynopsis: Grace "Grania" O'Malley, "the hussy who hath indeed impudently stepped o'er the bounds of womanhood", is the center character in playwright Maggie Cronin's story of the Irish pirate queen.     Set  against a backdrop of an Ireland soon to be lost forever, and Ireland on the cusp of history,  this solo piece performed by Christina Augello,  follows Grace from a young defiant  girl to her historic meeting  with England's Queen Elizabeth in 1593 at the age of 63.  Driven by a fervent love of the sea and a fierce loyalty to the Gaelic way of life, Grace became a "cut throat, cut purse sailor woman", a symbol of national defiance, "a nursemaid to every rebellion in Connaught".

More Pear Slices, please!  This new batch of deliciously varied short plays will work their magic on the season's Americana theme. And there's one more reason to celebrate:  Slices 2011 will mark the Pear's sixtieth production--celebrate with us!
sTheaterAddress: 1220 Pear Avenue, Unit K, Mountain View, CA 94043

sSynopsis: Peter Asher is the legendary record producer, artist manager and 1/2 of British Invasion duo Peter & Gordon has a superb new multimedia show, which debuted in Los Angeles in December with a sold-out show at the Grammy Museum. The show mixes video clips, photos from his personal archive, storytelling from Peter's history with The Beatles, The Rolling Stones, James Taylor, Linda Ronstadt, and a host of other legends from his nearly 5 decades in the business. Live performances by Peter & full band.
showName: Peter Asher: A Musical Memoir of the '60s and Beyond

sSynopsis: Come join the ladies behind PianoFight's Monday Night ForePlays as they hatch a compilation of brand-new comedic sketches in Spring EGGstravaganza this April!  ForePlays will premiere this original female-driven comedy variety show on April 4th at 8pm, and it will run every Monday night until April 25th at The Dark Room.    Brace yourselves, people; ForePlays has returned after a two-month hiatus to answer some of your most urgent and burning questions.  For example, ever wondered what would happen if the popular 5-Hour Energy product was re-imagined in a more adaptable 72-Hour form?  Or how the story of a 17th century humorist's poem about restoring hymens ("maiden-heads") can be told in a modern-day original musical?  And what is "dick bloat?"  "Spring EGGStravaganza" also tackles the age-old "chicken and the egg"dilemma - come first to learn which "came first!"
showName: PianoFight's Monday Night ForePlay's Spring EGGstravaganza

sSynopsis: Our first-ever new work for the mainstage! The shadow of Proposition 8 provides a rich backdrop for exploring the meaning of 'family.' Set in San Francisco, this original story will follow the paths, choices and challenges of Connor and his family and friends--gay and straight--as he comes to terms with himself and the world in which he lives.

Courthouse Center for the Arts will host the Rhode Island Tap Ensemble's Tribute to the King of Pop, Michael Jackson.    This dance concert will feature original choreography of RITE members as well as Michael Jackson original choreography.
showName: RI Tap Ensemble Tribute to Michael Jackson
theater: Court House Center for the Arts

sSynopsis: Our Americana season ends with a play about beginnings - Lorraine Hansberry's startlingly fresh masterpiece about an African-American family claiming their piece of the American Dream: a home of their own. The first play by an African-American woman ever to be produced on Broadway, this resilient, moving, witty work breathes fire and radiates hope, today more than ever.
sTheaterAddress: 1220 Pear Avenue, Unit K, Mountain View, CA 94043

sSynopsis: On her wedding day, Shelby is a vision in pink - two lovely shades! Her mother and friends gather at Truvy's Beauty Salon to prepare for the big day. Still, beauty, hairspray, and all the pink in the world can't protect this young woman from what lies ahead.    Brian Mertes directs this classic American comedy, written by Robert Harling.

Paint it Red! The passionate play that swept Broadway comes to Berkeley Rep, staged by acclaimed Associate Artistic Director Les Waters. At the height of his fame, Mark Rothko struggles in his studio to finish a major series of murals. The brilliant master wrestles with his new apprentice in a battle of wits over a bucket of paint. John Logan, the Oscar-nominated author of Aviator and Gladiator, won Tony and Drama Desk Awards for this feverish 90-minute drama that spans the spectrum of human emotion. From grief and fury to joy and hope, it's all covered in Red.

This free public performance is part of the Rotunda Dance Series, a partnership between Dancers' Group and World Arts West with San Francisco's Grants for the Arts and San Francisco City Hall. This month's featured artist, Hui Tama Nui, a dance company which was formed to preserve the Tahitian culture and its valued traditions while simultaneously aspiring to combine youthful energy and avant-garde style to Tahitian performances. Join us for their dramatic lunchtime dance performance amidst the grandeur of San Francisco City Hall--Friday, May 6, 2011 at noon.    The high profile Rotunda Dance Series brings the Bay Area's most acclaimed dance companies to San Francisco City Hall's rotunda space for free noon-time performances taking place the first Friday of each month. Events primarily involve dance, but might also include live music, theater or other performing art disciplines.
sTheaterAddress: 1 Dr Carlton B Goodlett Pl, San Francisco, CA 94102
showName: Rotunda Dance Series: Hui Tama Nui

sSynopsis: Author-director David Valayre's Sea Turtles is about three generations of women migrating between Tunis and Paris. The production challenges the notions of chronology and distance. Seven actresses interpret four characters at different ages; Tunis, Paris, a beach, a garret, a train and a road are evoked simultaneously on a single stage. Paris 1942 talks to Paris 1968. A grandmother sees the younger woman she once was.
showName: Sea Turtles: Three Generations of Women Cross the Mediterranean

sSynopsis: The Cold War turns hot in Cole Porter's final Broadway musical Silk Stockings, a sly and sophisticated musical version of the classic film Ninotchka.    Ninotchka, a stern Russian commissar (communist party official), is seduced by the joys of Paris and the charms of an American film agent, Steve Canfield. Wacky Hollywood star Janice Dayton, a Russian composer and three errant commissars add to the merrymaking.

An American entrepreneur has found the perfect Scottish island on which to build his new golf course. But as secrets -- and bodies -- are unearthed, the true nature of the island wreaks comic havoc. Artistic Director Christopher Ashley directs the world premiere of acclaimed playwright Arthur Kopit and Anton Dudley's supernatural comedy.
sTheaterAddress: 2910 La Jolla Village Drive, La Jolla, CA 92039

sSynopsis: The pressure is on for Scottish playwright J.M. Barrie -- his last play was an abysmal failure and his career is threatened by crippling writers block. In the nick of time, a chance meeting in a London park with a woman and her spirited young boys provides just the inspiration he needs. Based on the 2004 Academy Award-nominated film -- adapted from Allan Knee's play, The Man Who Was Peter Pan -- this world premiere musical tells the enchanting story of the real boys who inspired a literary masterpiece.
sTheaterAddress: 2910 La Jolla Village Drive, La Jolla, CA 92039

sSynopsis: Based on the legendary Broadway musical (1958), popular movie (1961), and modern revival (2002), Flower Drum Song follows Mei-Li, who flees Mao's Communist China and immigrates to San Francisco in the 1950s. She struggles to balance tradition and assimilation while looking for love. It also explores intergenerational conflict as Wang, the owner of an old-fashioned opera house, resists his son who wants to turn it into a nightclub in pursuit of the American dream.
sTheaterAddress: 2910 La Jolla Village Drive, La Jolla, CA 92039
showName: Flower Drum Song: A Musical Revival in Concert

sSynopsis: Based on the legendary Broadway musical (1958), popular movie (1961), and  modern revival (2002), Flower Drum Song follows Mei-Li, who flees Mao's  Communist China and immigrates to San Francisco in the 1950s. She struggles to  balance tradition and assimilation while looking for love. It also explores  intergenerational conflict as Wang, the owner of an old-fashioned opera house,  resists his son who wants to turn it into a nightclub in pursuit of the American  dream.
sTheaterAddress: 2910 La Jolla Village Drive, La Jolla, CA 92039
showName: Flower Drum Song: A Musical Revival in Concert

sSynopsis: Stuck in dead-end town and ignored by her family, 16-year-old Annie decides to create her own future by entering into a pregnancy pact with two of her high school friends. With savage humor and gritty poetry, Kirsten Greenidge's new play explores the challenges of choosing between the safety of the life you know and the danger of the life you desire.
sTheaterAddress: 2910 La Jolla Village Drive, La Jolla, CA 92039

sSynopsis: Join the world's most famous wanderer Peer Gynt as he dreams, swindles and charms his way through life in an exhilarating quest for fame and fortune. Five actors perform this theatrical adaptation of Ibsen's sweeping epic on stage full of inventive surprises. Satisfy your waderlust in this wild, funny, picaresque journey.
sTheaterAddress: 2910 La Jolla Village Drive, La Jolla, CA 92039

sSynopsis: Rafta, Rafta... takes a hilarious look at the generational divide on sex and marriage within a close-knit Indian family living in London. Following their wedding, two newlyweds find that starting their life together under the groom's family's roof is no honeymoon. With warmth and humor, this British comedy examines what happens when a young couple must choose between saving money or their marriage.

When a father brings his sleeping daughter in to a sleep disorder clinic, staff and patients mysteriously find themselves sharing the same dream. With beguiling characters, hypnotic lyrics, and a rocking score from GrooveLily, this musical about a father, a daughter and an unlikely suitor dives into the magical space between dreaming and waking.
sTheaterAddress: 2910 La Jolla Village Drive, La Jolla, CA 92039

sSynopsis: Real people. Real emotions. Really riveting improvisation. Featuring a rotating ensemble cast, including some of Chicago's finest actors.  Meisner actors master the art of being in the moment. Using the repetition exercise, our ensemble of actors have created a new form of improvisation--one that heightens the risk. Want to know what happens when we live truthfully, in the moment, in public? Watch. We strip it down--no imaginary circumstances. The Acting Tank is real people, real emotions, really riveting improvisation.     A rotating cast, led by Eileen Vorbach, takes the stage to give you a series of unscripted scenes governed by truthful human impulses. Are you brave enough to jump in? Come witness The Acting Tank.

A world premiere CST commission based on Carlo Collodi's classic tale of a wooden puppet who yearns to be a real boy, The Adventures of Pinocchio is a puppet-filled family musical that will turn CST's Courtyard Theater stage into a larger-than-life, European-style marionette theater. Creators Neil Bartram and Brian Hill garnered four Drama Desk Award nominations for The Story of My Life, which premiered on Broadway in 2009, and have collaborated on a number of other musicals, including Somewhere in the World/i>, The Nightingale and the Rose and Not Wanted on the Voyage./i> Rachel Rockwell returns to direct after staging the CST-commissioned world premiere musical The Emperor's New Clothes/i> last summer.

This year, Alvin Ailey American Dance Theater celebrates the 50th anniversary of Alvin Ailey's Revelations! There's never been a better time to experience the grace, artistry and athleticism of America's "Cultural Ambassador to the World."    Wednesday Evening, Saturday/Sunday Matinée(120 min) :  Anointed, The Evolution of A Secured Feminine, The Hunt, Revelations    Thursday/Friday Evening(130 min):  Night Creature, In/Side, Forgotten Time, Revelations    Saturday Evening(120 min):  Three Black Kings, Suite Otis, In/Side,  Revelations    Programs subject to change.

The Architecture & Design Film Festival makes its Chicago debut with screenings of more than 40 films from 11 different countries.  The Architecture and Design Film Festival, first held in October 2010 at the Tribeca Cinemas in New York City, is an annual event that celebrates the creative spirit of architecture and design through a dynamic program of films, panel discussions and Q&As with filmmakers, architects and designers.      Highlights of the Festival include the opening night screening of "How Much Does Your Building Weigh, Mr. Foster?" as well as screenings of "Studio Gang Architects: Aqua Tower," and "My Playground" with Danish Architect Bjarke Ingels.

Shaw's Arms and the Man explodes all our myths about love and war. The usual views of romance and battle are shown up for the ridiculous shams that they really are.  Bluntschli, the pragmatic outsider, educates the Accidental Hero, Sergius, and the operatically inclined heroine, Raina, in the ways of the real world, and changes their Bulgarian social landscape at the same time.  Life is not as it's portrayed in romantic novels.  It's more serious, and also a lot funnier.

Anne Kelly needs help. She's pushing 40 and still lives with her mother. Her deadbeat brother  won't even return her calls and the ancient family home seems to be falling down around her.  When Levi, a sweet but dim-witted younger man, comes into her life, Anne begins to see the  upside of not always being the grown up.

Ten years out of high school, three unhappy friends show up "not-quite-invited" to their classmate's hotel room for the perfect bachelorette celebration. Half a bathtub of booze later, the former prom queen is melting down, the nice-girl cokehead is on a mission to mend the mauled wedding dress, and the lacerating maid of honor finds her picture-perfect life less stable than it seemed. A smash hit Off Broadway, Leslye Headland's shrewd and biting play is an aria to the anxiety and self-loathing of a generation.

Before and After explores a single character's development in the aftermath of a life-changing event, played out in parallel with the story that them there in the first place. Life is defined in moments, but no one ever really changes.

In this darkly comical new work from the acclaimed playwright Martin McDonagh, the mysterious gun-toting Carmichael has been searching for his missing left hand for decades. Enter two bickering lovebirds with a hand to sell, and a hotel clerk with an aversion to gunfire, and soon life and death are up for grabs.  A Behanding in Spokane turns over American daily existence, exposing the obsessions, prejudices, madness, horrors, and above all, the absurdities that crawl beneath it.

What if God told you to be a better person but the world wouldn't allow it? Such is the dilemma  facing John Smith, a run-of-the-mill white-collar businessman who survives an office shooting and  is subsequently touched by what he believes to be a divine vision. His journey toward personal  enlightenment--past greed, lust and the other deadly sins--turns tense, hilarious, profane, and  heartbreaking. Exploring the narrow path to spiritual fulfillment, strewn with the funny, frantic failings of humankind, The Break of Noon showcases Neil LaBute at his discomforting best.

Porchlight Music Theatre presents the Chicago Premiere of A Catered Affair, a bittersweet reflection on the complexities of relationships between husbands and wives and parents and children. A couple must decide whether to spend their life savings on a family business or to celebrate their only daughter's marriage with a lavish catered affair, providing her with the joyful wedding they never had for themselves. A beautiful exploration of the resilience of love, A Catered Affair features a melodious, 50s-inspired score.

A lost gem from the early days of American realism, and it kicks off City Lit's five-year commemoration of the Civil War during its sesquicentennial years 2011-2015. Augustus Thomas' play follows an Illinois man from the early days of the war through the turn of the 20th century, as he carries the weight of his town's disapproval for his Southern sympathies.
sTheaterAddress: 1020 W. Bryn Mawr Avenue, Chicago, IL 60660
sTicketPrice: $25.00 during the regular run; $18.00 during previews

sSynopsis: A citywide cast of CPS high school teachers and students comes together to stage an adaptation of Shakespeare's The Taming of the Shrew in Chicago Shakespeare's annual collaboration with Chicago Public Schools. CPS Shakespeare! is an integral part of the Theater's Team Shakespeare performing arts-in-education program, which serves nearly 50,000 students annually, introducing Shakespeare's legacy to a new generation.
showName: CPS Shakespeare! The Taming of the Shrew

sSynopsis: Artistic Director Barbara Gaines brings her masterful hand to this contemporary play re-imagining Shakespeare's time. On the eve of the beheading of her court favorite and rumored lover, the Earl of Essex, Queen Elizabeth was entertained by a royal command performance by Shakespeare and his company. Upon this obscure historical fact, one of Canada's most acclaimed playwrights, Timothy Findley, imagines this daring and original drama. Longing for distraction, the Queen visits the acting troupe's lodgings, where she finds the actor who plays Shakespeare's leading ladies. In their passionate confrontation, the actor and the Queen come to shocking revelations about sexuality, identity and love.

Dixie's Tupperware Party  stars Dixie Longate, as the fast talking Tupperware Lady, who has packed up her catalogues and left her children in an Alabama trailer park to journey across America.     Critics  and audiences have howled with laughter as Dixie  throws a  good ol' fashioned Tupperware Party filled with outrageously funny tales, heartfelt accounts, FREE giveaways audience  participation and the most fabulous assortment of Tupperware ever sold on a theater stage! Loaded with the most up-to-date products available for purchase, Longate will share how she became the number one Tupperware seller in the world, as she educates her guests on the many alternative uses she has discovered for her plastic products.

Emotives is an improvised three-act play in miniature.  The show explores how the expression of feelings through language compels decisions and ultimately influences the lives of characters. What happens when we finally say what we mean?

In her 2005 play Eurydice, Sarah Ruhl re-imagines the classic Greek myth from its heroine's perspective. After dying on her wedding day, Eurydice finds herself in the underworld, her memory washed away in the River of Forgetfulness. She reunites with her father, matches wits with three petulant Stones, and struggles against the Lord of the Underworld. Ruhl's play is a fresh and lyrical look at a timeless love story.

Associate Artistic Director Gary Griffin continues a decade-long exploration of the Sondheim canon at CST with this valentine to a bygone era of the American musical theater, performed by an ensemble of 40 actors and musicians. On the eve of a crumbling theater's demolition, the legendary "Weismann Follies" company reunites to relive their moments in the spotlight. The production's Broadway premiere garnered seven Tony Awards, including Best Score, and gave birth to the classic standards "Broadway Baby," "I'm Still Here" and "Losing My Mind."

It's 1930 in Indiana and five young people are eager to break out of their small town. They need a car. They have a gun. But years later, contradictory memories are all that's left of their grand plans.     The Gospel According to James is based on the double lynching immortalized by the iconic Lawrence Beitler photograph. The play creates a fictional meeting between the man who survived the lynching and the only woman with them that night.     As The Gospel According to James dramatizes the events leading up to the crime, it also explores how unreliable personal memory underlies what we believe to be an immutable public history.     The play features two-time Tony nominated actor Andre De Shields.

Johnny Boy's Graduation is an interactive comedy like Tony n' Tina's Wedding where the audience are the guests at the event - Johnny's getting out of jail and the Boss is throwing a surprise party. Tensions are high because of missing loot and who will be the next boss. These gangsters have more issues than National Geographic.    Tickets include dinner and dancing.  Cash bar.  Not appropriate for children.

Brianna Borger will star as Anna, reprising the role she played in the production's Asian Tour, and Wayne Hu will star as the King of Siam, reprising his role most recently from the Allenberry Playhouse in Pennsylvania. Musical Director Eugene Dizon (Jeff Award for Porchlight's Ragtime) and Allison Hendrix will perform a new two-piano arrangement of the score, with one piano on each side of the stage as a symbolic representation of the meeting of two worlds.  The King and I is directed by L. Walter Stearns, who is concluding his successful tenure as Artistic Director of Porchlight Music Theatre after 12 years.
sTicketPrice: $38.00 per person, discounts for seniors, students, and groups available

sSynopsis: Callimaco loves Lucrezia, Lucrezia is married to Nicia, Nicia wants a baby… enter Ligurio and add a corrupt priest, the doting mother and the root of the mandrake to make for an extraordinarily complicated and hilarious plan. With everyone behaving so badly, can anyone possibly win?
Stephen Sondheim's 1981 musical: Book by George Furth; based on George F. Kaufman and Moss Hart's 1934 play of the same name!
sTheaterAddress: 1850 Green Bay Road, Highland Park, IL 60035

sSynopsis: What responsibility do artists have for the impact of their work? Provocative New York playwright and Pulitzer Prize finalist Adam Rapp offers a powerful portrait of small-town censorship and the American divide over family values in his newest play fresh from a sold-out Off-Broadway run, The Metal Children. A gifted New York writer attempts to defend his young adult novel to the same small American town hell bent on banning his work, causing an explosive encounter from which no one in the small Midwestern town will recover.

Following his acclaimed Chicago Shakespeare production of As You Like It, Associate Artistic Director Gary Griffin takes on Shakespeare's spectacular tale of fairies and paramours. When a quartet of mismatched lovers and a gaggle of hapless actors cross paths with the king and queen of the fairies beneath the boughs of an enchanted wood, they experience the inexplicable magic of falling in love--and the wonder of waking up from the sweetest of dreams.

Chicago Shakespeare Theater (CST) premieres Murder for Two--A Killer Musical, created by Joe Kinosian (music/book) and Kellen Blair (lyrics/book), Upstairs at Chicago Shakespeare.     This comedic Agatha Christie-like whodunit musical comes with a surprising twist: one actor plays the inspector, the other plays all 10 suspects, and both play the piano.     Staged by CST veteran director David H. Bell, this 75-minute premiere features the show's co-creator Joe Kinosian playing the slew of hilarious would-be criminals and Chicago favorite Alan Schmuckler performing the role of the inspector.

Mikey O Comedy Productions announces the new theater run of comedian Sean Flannery's Never Been to Paris for spring 2011.  The multimedia solo show features several hilarious stories of near-death experiences, all from trying to live life to the fullest.
